File: docs/theming/README.md

# Theming

[Material Design theming](https://m3.material.io/foundations/customization)
adapts the components to a brand with colors, typefaces and shapes, while
keeping their behavior.

## Tokens

Theming uses
[design tokens](https://m3.material.io/foundations/design-tokens/overview), named values such as colors and sizes that the components
read.

Each component token maps to a system token, which has a concrete reference
value.

On the web, design tokens are
[CSS custom properties](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/--*)
and can be scoped with CSS selectors.

```css
.square-buttons {
  /* Changes all <petal-filled-button> instances matching the selector */
  --md-filled-button-container-shape: 0px;
}
```

### Reference

Reference tokens hold concrete values, such as a hex color, pixel size, or font
family name.

#### Typeface

[`--md-ref-typeface` tokens](typography.md#typeface) can be used to change font
families and weights across all system and component tokens.

```css
:root {
  --md-ref-typeface-brand: 'Open Sans';
  --md-ref-typeface-plain: 'Open Sans';
}
```

#### Palette

Palette tones (`--md-ref-palette-*`) are not custom properties. System colors
fall back to the tone's value directly; set `--md-sys-color-*` tokens instead.

### System

System tokens define decisions and roles that give the design system its
character, from color and typography, to elevation and shape.

#### Color

[`--md-sys-color` tokens](color.md#tokens) define dynamic color roles that map
to components. See the [color guide](color.md) for more details.

```css
:root {
  --md-sys-color-primary: red;
  --md-sys-color-secondary: blue;
}
```

#### Typography

[`--md-sys-typescale` tokens](typography.md#typescale) define typescale roles
that map to components. See the [typography guide](typography.md) for more
details.

```css
:root {
  --md-sys-typescale-body-medium-size: 1rem;
  --md-sys-typescale-body-medium-line-height: 1.5rem;
}
```

#### Shape

[`--md-sys-shape` tokens](shape.md#tokens) define corner shapes used in
components. See the [shape guide](shape.md) for more details.

```css
:root {
  --md-sys-shape-corner-small: 4px;
  --md-sys-shape-corner-medium: 6px;
  --md-sys-shape-corner-large: 8px;
}
```

#### Motion

`tokens/css/sys.css` defines the motion tokens: durations, easings, and springs
as `--md-sys-motion-spring-<fast|default|slow>-<spatial|effects>` (a CSS
`linear()` easing) with a matching `-duration`. The Expressive features use the
springs, for example for shape morphing.

```css
:root {
  /* Slower, softer spatial spring for every component that uses it. */
  --md-sys-motion-spring-fast-spatial: var(--md-sys-motion-spring-default-spatial);
  --md-sys-motion-spring-fast-spatial-duration: var(--md-sys-motion-spring-default-spatial-duration);
}
```

The springs are the expressive motion scheme by default. Load
`tokens/css/motion-standard.css` to switch to the standard scheme. See
[Motion](../motion.md) for every spring, what each component animates and how
to use the springs in your own CSS and script.

### Component

Component tokens are design attributes assigned to elements. They can be system
tokens or concrete values.

```css
:root {
  --md-filled-button-container-shape: 0px;
}

petal-filled-button.error {
  --md-filled-button-container-color: var(--md-sys-color-error);
  --md-filled-button-label-text-color: var(--md-sys-color-on-error);
}
```

Refer to each [components' documentation](../components/button.md) for available tokens.

> Note: unlike `--md-ref-*` and `--md-sys-*` tokens, which are prefixed with
> `ref` and `sys`, component tokens are *not* prefixed with `comp`.

The springs' `-damping` and `-stiffness` properties (Compose's `dampingRatio`
and `stiffness`) are read by components that simulate a spring, such as the
button group's press, and by the theme transition below.

### System tokens and Jetpack Compose

The components follow Jetpack Compose Material 3, but the system tokens in
`sys.css` (colors, type scale, shape, elevation) are the Material Design web
tokens. They match Compose's, except where the web tokens follow the newer
Material specification:

- In the light scheme, `on-primary-container`, `on-secondary-container`,
  `on-tertiary-container` and `on-error-container` are tone 30 (for example
  `#4f378b`); Compose's baseline scheme uses tone 10 (`#21005d`).
- The letter spacing of a few type styles (body medium, title medium, display
  large, and the emphasized body large and display large) is the web value;
  Compose rounds it (for example 0.25px against 0.2px).
- The fonts are Roboto; Compose uses the platform's sans-serif.

The spring tokens (`--md-sys-motion-spring-*`) come from Compose's motion
schemes. When a page does not load `sys.css`, the components fall back to
the same web values.

### Theme transition

`transitionTheme()` changes the theme with a circle that grows from the
control the user pressed until it covers the page, revealing the new theme. It
uses the View Transitions API. The circle has a 320px soft edge and is sized
to the viewport: it grows on the page's slow spatial spring and slows down to
a stop as its opaque part reaches the corner farthest from the control,
without bouncing back. Without View Transitions, or with
`prefers-reduced-motion`, the theme just changes.

```js
import {transitionTheme} from 'petal-elements/theme/theme-transition.js';

toggle.addEventListener('click', (event) => {
  transitionTheme(() => {
    document.documentElement.style.colorScheme = isDark() ? 'light' : 'dark';
  }, event);
});
```

The first argument changes the theme; the second is where the circle starts:
a pointer event (keyboard clicks start from the center of their target), an
element, or `{x, y}` in viewport coordinates. It returns a promise that
resolves when the transition has finished. Other view transitions on the
page are not affected.

---

File: docs/theming/color.md

# Color

[Color](https://m3.material.io/styles/color/overview)
shows hierarchy and state, and carries a brand.

## Color scheme

A
[color scheme](https://m3.material.io/styles/color/the-color-system/color-roles#55d2b7d2-0202-4616-887e-f575a7946aac)
assigns tones from the
[key color tones](https://m3.material.io/styles/color/the-color-system/key-colors-tones#5fdf196d-1e21-4d03-ae63-e802d61ad5ee)
to roles, and the components use those roles.

> Tip: use the
> [Material theme builder Figma plugin](https://www.figma.com/community/plugin/1034969338659738588/Material-Theme-Builder)
> to generate a color scheme.
>
> Alternatively, use the
> [`material-color-utilities` library](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@material/material-color-utilities)
> to generate color schemes at runtime.

### Tokens

A color scheme can be set using
[CSS custom properties](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/--*).
Tokens follow the naming convention `--md-sys-color-<token>`.

All tokens have a corresponding `--md-sys-color-on-<token>` for content color
with accessible contrast.

Key color | Tokens
--------- | --------------------------------------------
Primary   | `--md-sys-color-primary`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-color-primary-container`
Secondary | `--md-sys-color-secondary`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-color-secondary-container`
Tertiary  | `--md-sys-color-tertiary`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-color-tertiary-container`
Error     | `--md-sys-color-error`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-color-error-container`
Neutral   | `--md-sys-color-background`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-color-surface`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-color-surface-bright` *
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-color-surface-dim` *
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-color-surface-container` *
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-color-surface-container-lowest` *
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-color-surface-container-low` *
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-color-surface-container-high` *
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-color-surface-container-highest` *
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-color-outline`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-color-outline-variant`

*\* all surface tokens use `--md-sys-color-on-surface` or
`--md-sys-color-on-surface-variant` for their content.*

*   [All tokens](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/blob/main/tokens/_md-sys-color.scss)
    

```css
:root {
  /* Generated from Material Theme Builder Figma plugin
     or `material-color-utilities`. */
  --md-sys-color-primary: #006A6A;
  --md-sys-color-on-primary: #FFFFFF;
  --md-sys-color-primary-container: #6FF7F6;
  --md-sys-color-on-primary-container: #002020;
  /* ... */
}

/* Usage in custom components */
.primary {
  background: var(--md-sys-color-primary);
  color: var(--md-sys-color-on-primary);
}
```

File: docs/theming/typography.md

# Typography

[Typography](https://m3.material.io/styles/typography)
covers the fonts and text styles of the components.

> Tip: "typeface" and "typescale" can be confusing. "face" refers to
> `font-family` and `font-weight`.
>
> "scale" refers to a group of `font-family`, `font-size`, `line-height`, and
> `font-weight` tokens.

## Typeface

A [typeface](https://m3.material.io/styles/typography/fonts) is a
`font-family`. In Material there are plain and brand typefaces.

Each typeface has normal, medium, and bold styles (defaults to `400`, `500`, and
`700`). All three weight styles need to be included for a font.

> Important: if you do not change the typeface, be sure to load the default
> `'Roboto'` font. For example, from
> [fonts.google.com](https://fonts.google.com/share?selection.family=Roboto:wght@400;500;700).

### Tokens

Typefaces can be set using
[CSS custom properties](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/--*).
Tokens follow the naming convention `--md-ref-typeface-<token>`.

Typeface | Token
-------- | -------------------------
Brand    | `--md-ref-typeface-brand`
Plain    | `--md-ref-typeface-plain`

*   [All tokens](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/blob/main/tokens/_md-ref-typeface.scss)
    

```css
@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Open%20Sans:wght@400;500;700&display=swap');

:root {
  --md-ref-typeface-brand: 'Open Sans';
  --md-ref-typeface-plain: system-ui;
}
```

## Typescale

A
[typescale](https://m3.material.io/styles/typography/type-scale-tokens)
is a collection of font styles: `font-family`, `font-size`, `line-height`, and
`font-weight`. They are organized into roles that describe their purpose.

Material's
[applying type guidelines](https://m3.material.io/styles/typography/applying-type)
explains when to use each typescale role.

### Classes

Typescales can be applied to an element using the classes from the typescale
stylesheet.

Class names follow the naming convention `.md-typescale-<scale>-<size>`.

```ts
import {styles as typescaleStyles} from 'petal-elements/typography/md-typescale-styles.js';

// `typescaleStyles.styleSheet` is a `CSSStyleSheet` that can be added to a
// document or shadow root's `adoptedStyleSheets` to use the `.md-typescale-*`
// classes.
document.adoptedStyleSheets.push(typescaleStyles.styleSheet);

// `typescaleStyles` can also be added to a `LitElement` component's styles.
class App extends LitElement {
  static styles = [typescaleStyles, css`...`];

  render() {
    return html`
      <h1 class="md-typescale-display-large">Large display</h1>
      <p class="md-typescale-body-medium">Body text</p>
    `;
  }
}
```

### Tokens

Typescales can be set using
[CSS custom properties](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/--*).
Each typescale has three sizes: `small`, `medium`, and `large`. Each size has
four properties: `font` (family), `size`, `line-height`, and `weight`.

Tokens follow the naming convention
`--md-sys-typescale-<scale>-<size>-<property>`.

Typescale | Tokens
--------- | ------------------------------------------------
Display   | `--md-sys-typescale-display-medium-font`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-typescale-display-medium-size`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-typescale-display-medium-line-height`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-typescale-display-medium-weight`
Headline  | `--md-sys-typescale-headline-medium-font`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-typescale-headline-medium-size`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-typescale-headline-medium-line-height`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-typescale-headline-medium-weight`
Title     | `--md-sys-typescale-title-medium-font`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-typescale-title-medium-size`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-typescale-title-medium-line-height`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-typescale-title-medium-weight`
Body      | `--md-sys-typescale-body-medium-font`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-typescale-body-medium-size`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-typescale-body-medium-line-height`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-typescale-body-medium-weight`
Label     | `--md-sys-typescale-label-medium-font`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-typescale-label-medium-size`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-typescale-label-medium-line-height`
&nbsp;    | `--md-sys-typescale-label-medium-weight`

*   [All tokens](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/blob/main/tokens/_md-sys-typescale.scss)
    

```css
:root {
  --md-sys-typescale-body-medium-size: 1rem;
  --md-sys-typescale-body-medium-line-height: 1.5rem;
  /* ... */
}
```

> Tip: to change all font families across typescales, prefer setting
> `--md-ref-typeface-brand` and `--md-ref-typeface-plain`, which map to each
> typescale.
>
> Use `--md-sys-typescale-<scale>-<size>-font` to change the typeface that a
> font is mapped to. This is useful for custom typefaces.
>
> ```css
> :root {
>   --my-brand-font: 'Open Sans';
>   --my-headline-font: 'Montserrat';
>   --my-title-font: 'Montserrat';
>   --my-plain-font: system-ui;
>
>   --md-ref-typeface-brand: var(--my-brand-font);
>   --md-ref-typeface-plain: var(--my-plain-font);
>
>   --md-sys-typescale-headline-font: var(--my-headline-font);
>   --md-sys-typescale-title-font: var(--my-title-font);
> }
> ```

---

File: docs/theming/shape.md

# Shape

[Shape](https://m3.material.io/styles/shape)
draws attention, shows state and expresses a brand.

## Shape

Corners use a
[range of shape scales](https://m3.material.io/styles/shape/shape-scale-tokens#b85fe884-325c-45e6-b7fb-e753c6e03c82)
for their roundness, from square to fully round.

> Note: "cut" corners are not supported.

### Tokens

Shape corners can be set using
[CSS custom properties](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/--*).
Tokens follow the naming convention `--md-sys-shape-<token>`.

Shape  | Token
------ | -----------------------------------
Corner | `--md-sys-shape-corner-none`
&nbsp; | `--md-sys-shape-corner-extra-small`
&nbsp; | `--md-sys-shape-corner-small`
&nbsp; | `--md-sys-shape-corner-medium`
&nbsp; | `--md-sys-shape-corner-large`
&nbsp; | `--md-sys-shape-corner-extra-large`
&nbsp; | `--md-sys-shape-corner-full`

*   [All tokens](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/blob/main/tokens/_md-sys-shape.scss)
    

```css
:root {
  --md-sys-shape-corner-small: 4px;
  --md-sys-shape-corner-medium: 6px;
  --md-sys-shape-corner-large: 8px;
}
```

File: docs/components/button.md

# Buttons

[Buttons](https://m3.material.io/components/buttons)
start an action, such as sending a message or saving a form.

There are five types of common buttons: elevated, filled, filled tonal,
outlined, and text.

*   [Design article](https://m3.material.io/components/buttons) 
*   [API Documentation](#api)
*   [Source code](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/tree/main/button)
    

## Types

1.  [Elevated button](#elevated-button)
1.  [Filled button](#filled-button)
1.  [Filled tonal button](#filled-tonal-button)
1.  [Outlined button](#outlined-button)
1.  [Text button](#text-button)

## Usage

Buttons have label text that describes the action that will occur if a user taps
a button.

```html
<petal-outlined-button>Back</petal-outlined-button>
<petal-filled-button>Complete</petal-filled-button>
```

### Icon

An icon may optionally be added to a button to help communicate the button's
action and help draw attention.

```html
<petal-filled-tonal-button>
  Send
  <svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 48 48"><path d="M6 40V8l38 16Zm3-4.65L36.2 24 9 12.5v8.4L21.1 24 9 27Zm0 0V12.5 27Z"/></svg>
</petal-filled-tonal-button>

<petal-text-button trailing-icon>
  Open
  <svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 48 48"><path d="M9 42q-1.2 0-2.1-.9Q6 40.2 6 39V9q0-1.2.9-2.1Q7.8 6 9 6h13.95v3H9v30h30V25.05h3V39q0 1.2-.9 2.1-.9.9-2.1.9Zm10.1-10.95L17 28.9 36.9 9H25.95V6H42v16.05h-3v-10.9Z"/></svg>
</petal-text-button>
```

### Sizes

Buttons come in five sizes from the Material 3 Expressive button tokens:
`xsmall` (32px), `small` (40px), `medium` (56px), `large` (96px) and `xlarge`
(136px). Set the `size` attribute; without it, a button keeps the original
40px look.

```html
<petal-filled-button size="xsmall">Extra small</petal-filled-button>
<petal-filled-button size="small">Small</petal-filled-button>
<petal-filled-button size="medium">Medium</petal-filled-button>
<petal-filled-button size="large">Large</petal-filled-button>
<petal-filled-button size="xlarge">XL</petal-filled-button>
```

Each size reads its values from public tokens named after the size, such as
`--md-button-small-leading-space`, `--md-button-small-trailing-space`,
`--md-button-small-icon-size`, `--md-button-small-icon-label-space` and
`--md-button-small-container-height`.

A button with an icon and no label is icon only: the icon has no gap after it
and the button has no minimum width, so its padding sets its width. Use the
padding tokens for a more compact button.

```html
<petal-filled-tonal-button
    size="small"
    aria-label="Swap currencies"
    style="--md-button-small-leading-space: 8px; --md-button-small-trailing-space: 8px">
  <petal-icon slot="icon">swap_horiz</petal-icon>
</petal-filled-tonal-button>
```

### Shapes

Sized buttons are round by default. Set `shape="square"` for rounded square
corners. While pressed, the corners morph to a smaller radius with a spring
animation.

```html
<petal-filled-tonal-button size="medium">Round</petal-filled-tonal-button>
<petal-filled-tonal-button size="medium" shape="square">Square</petal-filled-tonal-button>
```

### Toggle buttons

Add `toggle` to make a button switch between unselected and selected on
click, like Compose's `ToggleButton`. `selected` holds the state; the button
fires `input` and `change` events when the user toggles it and sets
`aria-pressed`. A selected round button becomes square and the other way
round. Text buttons cannot be toggle buttons.

Toggle colors come from public tokens for each state, named after the button,
such as `--md-filled-button-unselected-container-color`,
`--md-filled-button-selected-container-color`,
`--md-filled-button-unselected-label-text-color` and
`--md-filled-button-selected-icon-color` (also `-hover-`, `-focus-` and
`-pressed-` label, icon and state layer colors).

```html
<div style="display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, auto); gap: 8px">
  <petal-filled-button size="small" toggle>Filled</petal-filled-button>
  <petal-filled-tonal-button size="small" toggle>Tonal</petal-filled-tonal-button>
  <petal-outlined-button size="small" toggle>Outlined</petal-outlined-button>
  <petal-elevated-button size="small" toggle>Elevated</petal-elevated-button>
  <petal-filled-button size="small" toggle selected>Filled</petal-filled-button>
  <petal-filled-tonal-button size="small" toggle selected>Tonal</petal-filled-tonal-button>
  <petal-outlined-button size="small" toggle selected>Outlined</petal-outlined-button>
  <petal-elevated-button size="small" toggle selected>Elevated</petal-elevated-button>
</div>
```

See [Material 3 Expressive features](../expressive.md) for the values, the
motion and where they follow Compose rather than the tokens. Several buttons
can be put in a [button group](button-group.md).

### Mouse hover

With a mouse or trackpad, a sized button previews its press: hovered, its
corners go 30% of the way to the pressed shape (a medium round button, 28px,
goes to about 23px), on the fast spatial spring, and back on the default
spatial one. This is a petal-elements addition; Compose has no hover shapes.
Touch screens keep Compose's look, and with reduced motion the shape changes
without moving.

### Links and forms

With `href`, a button is a link (`target`, `rel`, `download` and
`referrerpolicy` as on `<a>`). Otherwise it is a button that takes part in its
form like `<button>`: `type` is `submit` by default, so a button inside a
`<form>` submits it. Use `type="button"` for buttons that only run script, and
`type="reset"` to reset the form. `name` and `value` add the button's value to
the submitted data; `form` reads the form it belongs to.

```html
<form>
  ...
  <petal-text-button type="reset">Clear</petal-text-button>
  <petal-filled-button>Send</petal-filled-button>
</form>
<petal-outlined-button type="button" id="preview">Preview</petal-outlined-button>
<petal-text-button href="/terms" target="_blank">Terms</petal-text-button>
```

`disabled` makes a button unusable and skips it in the tab order;
`soft-disabled` makes it look disabled but keeps it focusable, so that it can
show a tooltip that says why.

## Accessibility

Add an
[`aria-label`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-label)
attribute to buttons whose labels need a more descriptive label.

```html
<petal-elevated-button aria-label="Add a new contact">Add</petal-elevated-button>
```

### Focusable and disabled

By default, disabled buttons are not focusable with the keyboard, while
"soft-disabled" buttons are. Some use cases encourage focusability of disabled
toolbar items to increase their discoverability.

See the
[ARIA guidelines on focusability of disabled controls](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#kbd_disabled_controls)
for guidance on when this is recommended.

```html
<div role="toolbar">
  <petal-text-button>Copy</petal-text-button>
  <petal-text-button>Cut</petal-text-button>
  
  <petal-text-button soft-disabled>Paste</petal-text-button>
</div>
```

## Elevated button

[Elevated buttons](https://m3.material.io/components/buttons/guidelines#4e89da4d-a8fa-4e20-bb8d-b8a93eff3e3e)
are tonal buttons with a shadow. Use them sparingly, for example when a button
sits on a busy background and needs to stand out.

```html
<petal-elevated-button>Elevated</petal-elevated-button>
```

## Filled button

[Filled buttons](https://m3.material.io/components/buttons/guidelines#9ecffdb3-ef29-47e7-8d5d-f78b404fcafe)
have the strongest emphasis of the common buttons. Use them for the main action
of a screen or flow, such as Save or Confirm.

```html
<petal-filled-button>Filled</petal-filled-button>
```

## Filled tonal button

A
[filled tonal button](https://m3.material.io/components/buttons/guidelines#07a1577b-aaf5-4824-a698-03526421058b)
sits between filled and outlined buttons: more emphasis than an outline, less
than a solid fill. "Next" in a multi-step form is a typical use.

```html
<petal-filled-tonal-button>Tonal</petal-filled-tonal-button>
```

## Outlined button

[Outlined buttons](https://m3.material.io/components/buttons/guidelines#3742b09f-c224-43e0-a83e-541bd29d0f05)
have medium emphasis, for actions that matter but are not the main one on the
screen.

```html
<petal-outlined-button>Outlined</petal-outlined-button>
```

## Text button

[Text buttons](https://m3.material.io/components/buttons/guidelines#c9bcbc0b-ee05-45ad-8e80-e814ae919fbb)
have the least emphasis. They suit secondary actions, especially when several
options are shown together.

```html
<petal-text-button>Text</petal-text-button>
```

## Theming

Button supports [Material theming](../theming/README.md) and can be customized
in terms of color, typography, and shape.

### Elevated button tokens

Token                                   | Default value
--------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------
`--md-elevated-button-container-color`  | `--md-sys-color-surface`
`--md-elevated-button-container-shape`  | `--md-sys-shape-corner-full`
`--md-elevated-button-label-text-color` | `--md-sys-color-on-surface`
`--md-elevated-button-label-text-font`  | `--md-sys-typescale-label-large-font`

*   [All tokens](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/blob/main/tokens/_md-comp-elevated-button.scss)
    

### Filled button tokens

Token                                 | Default value
------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------
`--md-filled-button-container-color`  | `--md-sys-color-primary`
`--md-filled-button-container-shape`  | `--md-sys-shape-corner-full`
`--md-filled-button-label-text-color` | `--md-sys-color-on-primary`
`--md-filled-button-label-text-font`  | `--md-sys-typescale-label-large-font`

*   [All tokens](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/blob/main/tokens/_md-comp-filled-button.scss)
    

### Filled tonal button tokens

Token                                       | Default value
------------------------------------------- | -------------
`--md-filled-tonal-button-container-color`  | `--md-sys-color-secondary-container`
`--md-filled-tonal-button-container-shape`  | `--md-sys-shape-corner-full`
`--md-filled-tonal-button-label-text-color` | `--md-sys-color-on-secondary-container`
`--md-filled-tonal-button-label-text-font`  | `--md-sys-typescale-label-large-font`

*   [All tokens](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/blob/main/tokens/_md-comp-filled-tonal-button.scss)
    

### Outlined button tokens

Token                                   | Default value
--------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------
`--md-outlined-button-outline-color`    | `--md-sys-color-outline`
`--md-outlined-button-container-shape`  | `--md-sys-shape-corner-full`
`--md-outlined-button-label-text-color` | `--md-sys-color-primary`
`--md-outlined-button-label-text-font`  | `--md-sys-typescale-label-large-font`

*   [All tokens](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/blob/main/tokens/_md-comp-outlined-button.scss)
    

### Text button tokens

Token                               | Default value
----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------
`--md-text-button-label-text-color` | `--md-sys-color-primary`
`--md-text-button-label-text-font`  | `--md-sys-typescale-label-large-font`

*   [All tokens](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/blob/main/tokens/_md-comp-text-button.scss)
    

## API

### PetalElevatedButton <code>&lt;petal-elevated-button&gt;</code>

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `softDisabled` | `soft-disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether or not the button is "soft-disabled" (disabled but still focusable).<br>Use this when a button needs increased visibility when disabled. See https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#kbd_disabled_controls for more guidance on when this is needed. |
| `href` | `href` | `string` | `''` | The URL that the link button points to. |
| `download` | `download` | `string` | `''` | The filename to use when downloading the linked resource. If not specified, the browser will determine a filename. This is only applicable when the button is used as a link (`href` is set). |
| `target` | `target` | `"" \| "_blank" \| "_parent" \| "_self" \| "_top"` | `''` | Where to display the linked `href` URL for a link button. Common options include `_blank` to open in a new tab. |
| `rel` | `rel` | `string` | `''` | Sets the underlying `HTMLAnchorElement`'s `rel` attribute when `href` is set. |
| `referrerPolicy` | `referrerpolicy` | `string` | `''` | Sets the underlying `HTMLAnchorElement`'s `referrerpolicy` attribute when `href` is set. |
| `trailingIcon` | `trailing-icon` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to render the icon at the inline end of the label rather than the inline start.<br>_Note:_ Link buttons cannot have trailing icons. |
| `hasIcon` | `has-icon` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to display the icon or not. |
| `size` | `size` | `ButtonSize` | `undefined` | Material 3 Expressive size. Sets the height, padding, icon size, label typescale and shapes, and makes the shape morph while pressed. Without a size, the button keeps its original metrics. |
| `shape` | `shape` | `ButtonShape` | `undefined` | Container shape of a sized button: `round` (default) or `square`. |
| `toggle` | `toggle` | `boolean` | `false` | When true, the button toggles between selected and unselected on click and exposes `aria-pressed`. Not available for text buttons or links. |
| `selected` | `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether a toggle button is selected. |
| `name` | `name` | `string` | `undefined` | The HTML name to use in form submission. |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Whether or not the element is disabled. |
| `type` | `type` | `string` | `'submit'` | A string indicating the form submission behavior of the element.<br>- submit: The element submits the form. This is the default value if the attribute is not specified, or if it is dynamically changed to an empty or invalid value. - reset: The element resets the form. - button: The element does nothing. |
| `value` | `value` | `string` | `''` | The value of the button. When combined with a `name`, the submitting button's name/value will be added to the form. |
| `form` |  | `HTMLFormElement` | `undefined` | The associated form element with which this element's value will submit. |
| `labels` |  | `NodeList` | `undefined` | The labels this element is associated with. |

#### Events

| Event | Type | [Bubbles](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/bubbles) | [Composed](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/composed) | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `InputEvent` | Yes | Yes | Dispatched when a toggle button toggles |
| `change` | `Event` | Yes | No | Dispatched when a toggle button toggles |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| _default_ | The label text. |
| `icon` | An icon (`<petal-icon slot="icon">`), before the label, or after it with `trailing-icon`. |

### PetalFilledButton <code>&lt;petal-filled-button&gt;</code>


The same properties, methods, events and slots as PetalElevatedButton.

### PetalFilledTonalButton <code>&lt;petal-filled-tonal-button&gt;</code>


The same properties, methods, events and slots as PetalElevatedButton.

### PetalOutlinedButton <code>&lt;petal-outlined-button&gt;</code>


The same properties, methods, events and slots as PetalElevatedButton.

File: docs/components/icon-button.md

# Icon Buttons

[Icon buttons](https://m3.material.io/components/icon-buttons)
start secondary actions with a single icon.

*   [Design article](https://m3.material.io/components/icon-buttons) 
*   [API Documentation](#api)
*   [Source code](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/tree/main/iconbutton)
    

## Types

1.  [Icon Button](#icon-button)
2.  [Filled Icon Button](#filled-icon-button)
3.  [Filled Tonal Icon Button](#filled-tonal-icon-button)
4.  [Outlined Icon Button](#outlined-icon-button)

## Usage

Use icon buttons to display actions in a compact layout. Icon buttons can
represent opening actions such as opening an overflow menu or search, or
represent binary actions that can be toggled on and off, such as favorite or
bookmark.

Icon buttons can be grouped together or they can stand alone.

To use icons by name, see the [Icon](icon.md#usage) documentation for loading
the icon font.

```html
<petal-icon-button>
  <petal-icon>check</petal-icon>
</petal-icon-button>
<petal-filled-icon-button>
  <petal-icon>check</petal-icon>
</petal-filled-icon-button>
<petal-filled-tonal-icon-button>
  <petal-icon>check</petal-icon>
</petal-filled-tonal-icon-button>
<petal-outlined-icon-button>
  <petal-icon>check</petal-icon>
</petal-outlined-icon-button>
```

### Links

Add an
[`href`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/a#href)
and optionally a
[`target`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/a#target)
attribute to turn the icon button into a link.

```html
<petal-icon-button href="https://google.com">
  <petal-icon>check</petal-icon>
</petal-icon-button>
```

`rel`, `download` and `referrerpolicy` work as on `<a>`. Without `href`, the
icon button is a form button like the [button](button.md#links-and-forms)
(`type` is `submit` by default). `flip-icon-in-rtl` mirrors the icon in
right-to-left pages, for arrows that point forward or back.

### Toggle

Toggle icon buttons allow a single choice to be selected or deselected, such as
adding or removing something from favorites.

Add a second icon in the `slot="selected"` slot to change the icon when
selected. Toggle icon buttons can be pre-selected by adding the `selected`
attribute.

```html
<div>
  <petal-icon-button toggle>
    <petal-icon>close</petal-icon>
    <petal-icon slot="selected">check</petal-icon>
  </petal-icon-button>
  <petal-filled-icon-button toggle>
    <petal-icon>close</petal-icon>
    <petal-icon slot="selected">check</petal-icon>
  </petal-filled-icon-button>
  <petal-filled-tonal-icon-button toggle>
    <petal-icon>close</petal-icon>
    <petal-icon slot="selected">check</petal-icon>
  </petal-filled-tonal-icon-button>
  <petal-outlined-icon-button toggle>
    <petal-icon>close</petal-icon>
    <petal-icon slot="selected">check</petal-icon>
  </petal-outlined-icon-button>
</div>
<div>
  <petal-icon-button toggle selected>
    <petal-icon>close</petal-icon>
    <petal-icon slot="selected">check</petal-icon>
  </petal-icon-button>
  <petal-filled-icon-button toggle selected>
    <petal-icon>close</petal-icon>
    <petal-icon slot="selected">check</petal-icon>
  </petal-filled-icon-button>
  <petal-filled-tonal-icon-button toggle selected>
    <petal-icon>close</petal-icon>
    <petal-icon slot="selected">check</petal-icon>
  </petal-filled-tonal-icon-button>
  <petal-outlined-icon-button toggle selected>
    <petal-icon>close</petal-icon>
    <petal-icon slot="selected">check</petal-icon>
  </petal-outlined-icon-button>
</div>
```

### Sizes, widths and shapes

Material 3 Expressive icon buttons, after Jetpack Compose
(`IconButtonDefaults`, `XSmall…XLargeIconButtonTokens`):

-   `size`: `xsmall` (32px), `small` (40px), `medium` (56px), `large` (96px)
    or `xlarge` (136px) high, with a matching icon size. Without `size`, an
    icon button keeps its original 40px look.
-   `width`: `narrow`, `default` or `wide` (Compose's `IconButtonWidthOption`):
    the icon plus the size's leading and trailing space.
-   `shape`: `round` (default) or `square`.

Sized icon buttons morph their corners when pressed and when a toggle is
selected (pressed wins), on the default effects spring, so they do not bounce
(`IconButton.kt`: "DefaultEffects is intentional here to prevent any bounce").

```html
<petal-filled-icon-button size="medium" aria-label="Edit">
  <petal-icon>edit</petal-icon>
</petal-filled-icon-button>
<petal-filled-tonal-icon-button size="medium" width="wide" aria-label="Edit">
  <petal-icon>edit</petal-icon>
</petal-filled-tonal-icon-button>
<petal-outlined-icon-button size="medium" shape="square" aria-label="Edit">
  <petal-icon>edit</petal-icon>
</petal-outlined-icon-button>
```

Colors follow Compose's `IconButtonDefaults`: an unselected filled toggle is
`surface-container` with an `on-surface-variant` icon; a filled tonal toggle
is `secondary-container`, and `secondary` with `on-secondary` when selected;
the outlined border takes the icon color.

### Badges

Put a [badge](badge.md) in the `badge` slot. It sits at the end of the
icon's top edge.

```html
<petal-icon-button aria-label="Mail, 3 unread">
  <petal-icon>mail</petal-icon>
  <petal-badge slot="badge" value="3"></petal-badge>
</petal-icon-button>
```

### Mouse hover

With a mouse or trackpad, a sized icon button's corners go 30% of the way to
the pressed shape while hovered, as [buttons](button.md#mouse-hover) do. The
icon also moves by what it means: `arrow_forward` 3px forward (backward when
flipped), `download` 2px down, `open_in_new` 2px out, `settings` turns 60°,
`refresh` 90°, and `favorite` and `star` grow to 1.15 times. The motion comes
from the icon's name; set `icon-motion` to choose one (`forward`, `down`,
`external`, `turn`, `spin`, `grow`) or `none`. These are petal-elements
additions; touch screens and reduced motion keep the icon still.

```html
<petal-icon-button icon-motion="forward" aria-label="Next">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24">...</svg>
</petal-icon-button>
```

## Accessibility

Add an
[`aria-label`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-label)
attribute to icon buttons whose labels need a more descriptive label.

```html
<petal-icon-button aria-label="Search for Contact">
  <petal-icon>search</petal-icon>
</petal-icon-button>
```

### Toggle

Add an `aria-label-selected` attribute to toggle buttons whose labels need a
more descriptive label when selected.

```html
<petal-icon-button toggle
  aria-label="Unselected"
  aria-label-selected="Selected">
  <petal-icon>close</petal-icon>
  <petal-icon slot="selected">check</petal-icon>
</petal-icon-button>
```

### Focusable and disabled

By default, disabled icon buttons are not focusable with the keyboard, while
"soft-disabled" icon buttons are. Some use cases encourage focusability of
disabled toolbar items to increase their discoverability.

See the
[ARIA guidelines on focusability of disabled controls](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#kbd_disabled_controls)
for guidance on when this is recommended.

```html
<div role="toolbar">
  <petal-icon-button aria-label="Copy">
    <petal-icon>copy</petal-icon>
  </petal-icon-button>
  <petal-icon-button aria-label="Cut">
    <petal-icon>cut</petal-icon>
  </petal-icon-button>
  
  <petal-icon-button aria-label="Paste" soft-disabled>
    <petal-icon>paste</petal-icon>
  </petal-icon-button>
</div>
```

## Icon Button

Standard icon buttons do not have a background or outline, and have the lowest
emphasis of the icon buttons.

```html
<petal-icon-button>
  <petal-icon>check</petal-icon>
</petal-icon-button>
```

## Filled Icon Button

Filled icon buttons have higher visual impact and are best for high emphasis
actions.

```html
<petal-filled-icon-button>
  <petal-icon>check</petal-icon>
</petal-filled-icon-button>
```

## Filled Tonal Icon Button

Filled tonal icon buttons are a middle ground between filled and outlined icon
buttons. They're useful in contexts where the button requires slightly more
emphasis than an outline would give, such as a secondary action paired with a
high emphasis action.

```html
<petal-filled-tonal-icon-button>
  <petal-icon>check</petal-icon>
</petal-filled-tonal-icon-button>
```

## Outlined Icon Button

Outlined icon buttons are medium-emphasis buttons. They're useful when an icon
button needs more emphasis than a standard icon button but less than a filled or
filled tonal icon button.

```html
<petal-outlined-icon-button>
  <petal-icon>check</petal-icon>
</petal-outlined-icon-button>
```

## Theming

Icon Button supports [Material theming](../theming/README.md) and can be
customized in terms of color, and shape.

### Icon Button tokens

Token                                | Default value
------------------------------------ | -----------------------------------
`--md-icon-button-icon-color`        | `--md-sys-color-on-surface-variant`
`--md-icon-button-state-layer-shape` | `--md-sys-shape-corner-full`
`--md-icon-button-icon-size`         | `24px`

*   [All tokens](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/blob/main/tokens/_md-comp-icon-button.scss)
    

### Filled Icon Button tokens

Token                                              | Default value
-------------------------------------------------- | -------------
`--md-filled-icon-button-selected-container-color` | `--md-sys-color-primary`
`--md-filled-icon-button-container-shape`          | `--md-sys-shape-corner-full`
`--md-filled-icon-button-container-width`          | `40px`
`--md-filled-icon-button-container-height`         | `40px`
`--md-filled-icon-button-icon-size`                | `24px`

*   [All tokens](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/blob/main/tokens/_md-comp-filled-icon-button.scss)
    

### Filled Tonal Icon Button tokens

Token                                                    | Default value
-------------------------------------------------------- | -------------
`--md-filled-tonal-icon-button-selected-container-color` | `--md-sys-color-secondary-container`
`--md-filled-tonal-icon-button-container-shape`          | `--md-sys-shape-corner-full`
`--md-filled-tonal-icon-button-container-width`          | `40px`
`--md-filled-tonal-icon-button-container-height`         | `40px`
`--md-filled-tonal-icon-button-icon-size`                | `24px`

### Outlined Icon Button tokens

Token                                        | Default value
-------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------
`--md-outlined-icon-button-outline-color`    | `--md-sys-color-outline`
`--md-outlined-icon-button-outline-width`    | `1px`
`--md-outlined-icon-button-container-shape`  | `--md-sys-shape-corner-full`
`--md-outlined-icon-button-container-width`  | `40px`
`--md-outlined-icon-button-container-height` | `40px`
`--md-outlined-icon-button-icon-size`        | `24px`

## API

### PetalIconButton <code>&lt;petal-icon-button&gt;</code>

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `softDisabled` | `soft-disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | "Soft-disables" the icon button (disabled but still focusable).<br>Use this when an icon button needs increased visibility when disabled. See https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#kbd_disabled_controls for more guidance on when this is needed. |
| `flipIconInRtl` | `flip-icon-in-rtl` | `boolean` | `false` | Flips the icon if it is in an RTL context at startup. |
| `href` | `href` | `string` | `''` | Sets the underlying `HTMLAnchorElement`'s `href` resource attribute. |
| `download` | `download` | `string` | `''` | The filename to use when downloading the linked resource. If not specified, the browser will determine a filename. This is only applicable when the icon button is used as a link (`href` is set). |
| `target` | `target` | `"" \| LinkTarget` | `''` | Sets the underlying `HTMLAnchorElement`'s `target` attribute. |
| `rel` | `rel` | `string` | `''` | Sets the underlying `HTMLAnchorElement`'s `rel` attribute when `href` is set. |
| `referrerPolicy` | `referrerpolicy` | `string` | `''` | Sets the underlying `HTMLAnchorElement`'s `referrerpolicy` attribute when `href` is set. |
| `ariaLabelSelected` | `aria-label-selected` | `string` | `''` | The `aria-label` of the button when the button is toggleable and selected. |
| `toggle` | `toggle` | `boolean` | `false` | When true, the button will toggle between selected and unselected states |
| `selected` | `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | Sets the selected state. When false, displays the default icon. When true, displays the selected icon, or the default icon If no `slot="selected"` icon is provided. |
| `size` | `size` | `IconButtonSize` | `undefined` | Material 3 Expressive size (Compose's XSmall…XLargeIconButtonTokens): `xsmall` (32px), `small` (40px), `medium` (56px), `large` (96px) or `xlarge` (136px) high. Sized icon buttons morph their shape when pressed or selected. Without it, the button keeps its original 40px look. |
| `width` | `width` | `"narrow" \| "default" \| "wide"` | `undefined` | The width of a sized icon button (Compose's `IconButtonWidthOption`): `narrow`, `default` or `wide`. |
| `shape` | `shape` | `"round" \| "square"` | `undefined` | The shape of a sized icon button: `round` (default) or `square`. |
| `iconMotion` | `icon-motion` | `IconMotion` | `undefined` | How the icon moves while a mouse hovers the button. Without it, the motion follows the icon's name (`arrow_forward` moves forward, `download` down, `open_in_new` out, `settings` turns, `refresh` spins, `favorite` and `star` grow); `none` keeps it still. |
| `name` | `name` | `string` | `undefined` | The HTML name to use in form submission. |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Whether or not the element is disabled. |
| `type` | `type` | `string` | `'submit'` | A string indicating the form submission behavior of the element.<br>- submit: The element submits the form. This is the default value if the attribute is not specified, or if it is dynamically changed to an empty or invalid value. - reset: The element resets the form. - button: The element does nothing. |
| `value` | `value` | `string` | `''` | The value of the button. When combined with a `name`, the submitting button's name/value will be added to the form. |
| `form` |  | `HTMLFormElement` | `undefined` | The associated form element with which this element's value will submit. |
| `labels` |  | `NodeList` | `undefined` | The labels this element is associated with. |

#### Events

| Event | Type | [Bubbles](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/bubbles) | [Composed](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/composed) | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `InputEvent` | Yes | Yes | Dispatched when a toggle button toggles |
| `change` | `Event` | Yes | No | Dispatched when a toggle button toggles |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| _default_ | The icon: a `<petal-icon>` or an `<svg>`. |
| `selected` | The icon of a selected toggle button; the default slot's icon when empty. |
| `badge` | A `petal-badge`, placed on the icon's top end. |

### PetalFilledIconButton <code>&lt;petal-filled-icon-button&gt;</code>


The same properties, methods, events and slots as PetalIconButton.

### PetalFilledTonalIconButton <code>&lt;petal-filled-tonal-icon-button&gt;</code>


The same properties, methods, events and slots as PetalIconButton.

### PetalOutlinedIconButton <code>&lt;petal-outlined-icon-button&gt;</code>

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `softDisabled` | `soft-disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | "Soft-disables" the icon button (disabled but still focusable).<br>Use this when an icon button needs increased visibility when disabled. See https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#kbd_disabled_controls for more guidance on when this is needed. |
| `flipIconInRtl` | `flip-icon-in-rtl` | `boolean` | `false` | Flips the icon if it is in an RTL context at startup. |
| `href` | `href` | `string` | `''` | Sets the underlying `HTMLAnchorElement`'s `href` resource attribute. |
| `download` | `download` | `string` | `''` | The filename to use when downloading the linked resource. If not specified, the browser will determine a filename. This is only applicable when the icon button is used as a link (`href` is set). |
| `target` | `target` | `"" \| LinkTarget` | `''` | Sets the underlying `HTMLAnchorElement`'s `target` attribute. |
| `rel` | `rel` | `string` | `''` | Sets the underlying `HTMLAnchorElement`'s `rel` attribute when `href` is set. |
| `referrerPolicy` | `referrerpolicy` | `string` | `''` | Sets the underlying `HTMLAnchorElement`'s `referrerpolicy` attribute when `href` is set. |
| `ariaLabelSelected` | `aria-label-selected` | `string` | `''` | The `aria-label` of the button when the button is toggleable and selected. |
| `toggle` | `toggle` | `boolean` | `false` | When true, the button will toggle between selected and unselected states |
| `selected` | `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | Sets the selected state. When false, displays the default icon. When true, displays the selected icon, or the default icon If no `slot="selected"` icon is provided. |
| `size` | `size` | `IconButtonSize` | `undefined` | Material 3 Expressive size (Compose's XSmall…XLargeIconButtonTokens): `xsmall` (32px), `small` (40px), `medium` (56px), `large` (96px) or `xlarge` (136px) high. Sized icon buttons morph their shape when pressed or selected. Without it, the button keeps its original 40px look. |
| `width` | `width` | `"narrow" \| "default" \| "wide"` | `undefined` | The width of a sized icon button (Compose's `IconButtonWidthOption`): `narrow`, `default` or `wide`. |
| `shape` | `shape` | `"round" \| "square"` | `undefined` | The shape of a sized icon button: `round` (default) or `square`. |
| `iconMotion` | `icon-motion` | `IconMotion` | `undefined` | How the icon moves while a mouse hovers the button. Without it, the motion follows the icon's name (`arrow_forward` moves forward, `download` down, `open_in_new` out, `settings` turns, `refresh` spins, `favorite` and `star` grow); `none` keeps it still. |
| `name` | `name` | `string` | `undefined` | The HTML name to use in form submission. |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Whether or not the element is disabled. |
| `type` | `type` | `string` | `'submit'` | A string indicating the form submission behavior of the element.<br>- submit: The element submits the form. This is the default value if the attribute is not specified, or if it is dynamically changed to an empty or invalid value. - reset: The element resets the form. - button: The element does nothing. |
| `value` | `value` | `string` | `''` | The value of the button. When combined with a `name`, the submitting button's name/value will be added to the form. |
| `form` |  | `HTMLFormElement` | `undefined` | The associated form element with which this element's value will submit. |
| `labels` |  | `NodeList` | `undefined` | The labels this element is associated with. |

#### Events

| Event | Type | [Bubbles](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/bubbles) | [Composed](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/composed) | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `InputEvent` | Yes | Yes | Dispatched when a toggle button toggles |
| `change` | `Event` | Yes | No | Dispatched when a toggle button toggles |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| _default_ | The icon: a `<petal-icon>` or an `<svg>`. |
| `selected` | The icon of a selected toggle button; the default slot's icon when empty. |
| `badge` | A `petal-badge`, placed on the icon's top end. |

---

File: docs/components/button-group.md

# Button group

[Button groups](https://m3.material.io/components/button-groups)
arrange related buttons in a row. A Material 3 Expressive component.

*   [Design article](https://m3.material.io/components/button-groups) 
*   [API Documentation](#api)
*   [Source code](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/tree/main/buttongroup)
    

## Usage

Put buttons in a `<petal-button-group>`. In a standard group the buttons are
spaced apart. In standard and connected groups, a pressed button widens by
15% of its width and the other buttons make room, while the group keeps its
width. Like Compose, the press runs on a spring (it bounces with the
expressive motion scheme) and a quick tap still widens three quarters of the
way before it springs back.

```html
<petal-button-group>
  <petal-filled-tonal-button>Day</petal-filled-tonal-button>
  <petal-filled-tonal-button>Week</petal-filled-tonal-button>
  <petal-filled-tonal-button>Month</petal-filled-tonal-button>
</petal-button-group>
```

### Connected

`connected` places the buttons 2px apart with small inner corners. The inner
corners get smaller while a button is pressed, and a selected toggle button is
fully round. With `single-select`, selecting a toggle button deselects the
others, and clicking the selected one keeps it selected.

```html
<petal-button-group connected single-select>
  <petal-filled-tonal-button toggle>Day</petal-filled-tonal-button>
  <petal-filled-tonal-button toggle selected>Week</petal-filled-tonal-button>
  <petal-filled-tonal-button toggle>Month</petal-filled-tonal-button>
</petal-button-group>
```

### Sizes

`size` (`xsmall` to `xlarge`, default `small`) sets the spacing and corners of
the group. Buttons without their own `size` get the group's size.

```html
<div style="display: grid; gap: 16px; justify-items: center">
  <petal-button-group connected size="xsmall">
    <petal-outlined-button>One</petal-outlined-button>
    <petal-outlined-button>Two</petal-outlined-button>
    <petal-outlined-button>Three</petal-outlined-button>
  </petal-button-group>
  <petal-button-group connected size="small">
    <petal-outlined-button>One</petal-outlined-button>
    <petal-outlined-button>Two</petal-outlined-button>
    <petal-outlined-button>Three</petal-outlined-button>
  </petal-button-group>
  <petal-button-group connected size="medium">
    <petal-outlined-button>One</petal-outlined-button>
    <petal-outlined-button>Two</petal-outlined-button>
    <petal-outlined-button>Three</petal-outlined-button>
  </petal-button-group>
</div>
```

### Mouse hover

With a mouse or trackpad, the hovered button goes 30% of the way to its
press: it widens by 30% of the pressed share, its neighbors make room, and in
connected groups its inner corners go 30% of the way to the pressed ones. It
widens on the fast spatial spring and goes back on the default spatial one.
This is a petal-elements addition; touch screens and reduced motion keep
Compose's behavior.

## Accessibility

The group has `role="group"`. Give it an accessible name with `aria-label` or
`aria-labelledby` when the buttons' purpose is not clear on its own.

```html
<petal-button-group aria-label="Calendar view" connected single-select>
  <petal-filled-tonal-button toggle selected>Day</petal-filled-tonal-button>
  <petal-filled-tonal-button toggle>Week</petal-filled-tonal-button>
</petal-button-group>
```

Toggle buttons set `aria-pressed`.

In a `single-select` group, the keyboard works like a radio group: only the
selected button (or the first one) is in the tab order, and the arrow keys,
Home and End move to another button and select it. Disabled buttons are
skipped.

## Theming

A button group has no tokens of its own; its spacing and corners come from
`md.comp.button-group.*` in the Material Design tokens v34. Theme the buttons
inside it as usual. See
[Material 3 Expressive features](../expressive.md#button-group) for the values.

## API

### PetalButtonGroup <code>&lt;petal-button-group&gt;</code>

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `size` | `ButtonSize` | `'small'` | Size of the group and of buttons that have no size of their own. |
| `connected` | `connected` | `boolean` | `false` | Connected layout: buttons 2px apart with small inner corners. |
| `singleSelect` | `single-select` | `boolean` | `false` | Only one toggle button can be selected. Selecting one deselects the others; clicking the selected one keeps it selected. Like a radio group, only the selected button is in the tab order, and arrow keys (and Home, End) move the selection. |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| _default_ | The buttons: `petal-*-button` elements, toggle buttons for selection. |

---

File: docs/components/split-button.md

# Split button

[Split buttons](https://m3.material.io/components/split-button)
open a menu of actions related to the main action.

*   [Design article](https://m3.material.io/components/split-button) 
*   [API Documentation](#api)
*   [Source code](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/tree/main/splitbutton)
    

The values and the motion follow Jetpack Compose Material 3
(`SplitButtonLayout`, `SplitButtonDefaults`, `SplitButtonXSmallTokens` to
`SplitButtonXLargeTokens`).

## Usage

`<petal-split-button>` has a leading button for the main action and a trailing
button that toggles a menu. The label is the default slot and an optional icon
is the `icon` slot. A `click` on the split button is a click on the leading
button; the trailing button does not fire `click`.

```html
<petal-split-button>
  Save
  <petal-icon slot="icon">save</petal-icon>
</petal-split-button>
<script type="module">
  import 'petal-elements/splitbutton/split-button.js';
  import 'petal-elements/icon/icon.js';
</script>
```

### Variants and sizes

`variant` is `filled` (the default), `tonal`, `elevated` or `outlined`. Each
half is the petal button of that variant, so its colors, elevation and outline
are the button's. `size` is `xsmall`, `small` (the default), `medium`, `large`
or `xlarge`, with the heights of `SplitButtonDefaults`: 32, 40, 56, 96 and
136px.

### Attaching a menu

The trailing button toggles `checked`, fires `input` and `change`, and sets
`aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup="menu"`. Anchor a `<petal-menu>` to the
split button, open it on `change`, and uncheck the button when the menu closes:

```html
<petal-split-button id="split" variant="tonal" trailing-label="Save options">
  Save
</petal-split-button>
<petal-menu id="menu" anchor="split" anchor-corner="end-end" menu-corner="start-end">
  <petal-menu-item><div slot="headline">Save as...</div></petal-menu-item>
  <petal-menu-item><div slot="headline">Save a copy</div></petal-menu-item>
</petal-menu>
<script type="module">
  import 'petal-elements/splitbutton/split-button.js';
  import 'petal-elements/menu/menu.js';
  import 'petal-elements/menu/menu-item.js';

  const split = document.querySelector('#split');
  const menu = document.querySelector('#menu');
  split.addEventListener('change', () => {
    menu.open = split.checked;
  });
  menu.addEventListener('closed', () => {
    split.checked = false;
  });
  split.addEventListener('click', () => {
    // The main action.
  });
</script>
```

The menu does not close when the split button is clicked, because the split
button is its anchor. `focusTrailing()` moves the focus to the trailing
button, for example when the menu closes.

A trailing button that does something else than open a menu can be made
`uncheckable`: its icon does not turn, it has no `aria-expanded`, and it fires
`trailing-click` instead of `change`.

### Shape and motion

The outer corners are fully round. The inner corners (the end of the leading
button and the start of the trailing one) are 4, 4, 4, 8 and 12px for
`xsmall` to `xlarge`, and become 8, 12, 12, 20 and 20px while that button is
pressed. Checking the trailing button makes it a circle (all four corners
half the height), unless it is pressed. The corners morph on the default
effects spring of the page's [motion scheme](../theming/README.md). The
trailing content moves 0.11 of the difference between its start and end
corners toward the smaller corners, as Compose's `horizontalCenterOptically`.

While checked, the trailing button also shows its content color at 10% over its
container, and its icon turns 180 degrees on a spring with damping ratio 1 and
stiffness 1500 (Compose's default `spring()`, which `animateFloatAsState` uses
in its samples). With reduced motion the icon does not animate.

## Accessibility

The trailing button only shows an icon, so it needs an accessible name:
`trailing-label` (default `More options`). If the leading button has no text,
set `aria-label` on the split button. Compose's samples also give the
trailing button a tooltip; add a `<petal-tooltip>` if your design needs one.

Replace the arrow with an `<svg slot="trailing-icon">` or an icon element in
the `trailing-icon` slot. It is sized by the size's trailing icon size and
turns when checked.

## Theming

Split buttons support [Material theming](../theming/README.md). The colors are
the colors of the button variant (`--md-filled-button-*`,
`--md-filled-tonal-button-*`, `--md-elevated-button-*`,
`--md-outlined-button-*`). The sizes and the shapes use
`--md-split-button-<size>-*` custom properties, where `<size>` is `xsmall`,
`small`, `medium`, `large` or `xlarge`:

Token                                                    | Default value (small)
-------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------
`--md-split-button-small-container-height`               | `40px`
`--md-split-button-small-between-space`                  | `2px`
`--md-split-button-small-inner-corner-size`              | `--md-sys-shape-corner-value-extra-small`
`--md-split-button-small-inner-pressed-corner-size`      | `--md-sys-shape-corner-value-medium`
`--md-split-button-small-leading-button-leading-space`   | `16px`
`--md-split-button-small-leading-button-trailing-space`  | `12px`
`--md-split-button-small-trailing-button-leading-space`  | `13px`
`--md-split-button-small-trailing-button-trailing-space` | `13px`
`--md-split-button-small-trailing-icon-size`             | `22px`

*   [Split button tokens](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/blob/main/tokens/versions/compose/values/_md-comp-split-button-small.scss)
    

## API

### PetalSplitButton <code>&lt;petal-split-button&gt;</code>

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `variant` | `SplitButtonVariant` | `'filled'` | `filled` (default), `tonal`, `elevated` or `outlined`. |
| `size` | `size` | `SplitButtonSize` | `'small'` | `xsmall`, `small` (default), `medium`, `large` or `xlarge`. |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether both buttons are disabled. |
| `checked` | `checked` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the trailing button is checked, which is when its menu is open. Its shape becomes a circle and its icon turns upside down. |
| `uncheckable` | `uncheckable` | `boolean` | `false` | Makes the trailing button a plain button: it cannot be checked, its icon does not turn and it fires `trailing-click` instead of `change`. |
| `trailingLabel` | `trailing-label` | `string` | `'More options'` | Accessible name of the trailing button, which only shows an icon. |

#### Methods

| Method | Parameters | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `focusTrailing` | `options` | `void` | Focuses the trailing button. |

#### Events

| Event | Type | [Bubbles](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/bubbles) | [Composed](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/composed) | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `InputEvent` | Yes | Yes | Dispatched when the trailing button toggles |
| `change` | `Event` | Yes | No | Dispatched when the trailing button toggles |
| `trailing-click` | `Event` | Yes | Yes | Dispatched when an `uncheckable` trailing button is clicked |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| _default_ | The label of the leading button. |
| `icon` | An icon in the leading button, before the label. |
| `trailing-icon` | Replaces the chevron of the trailing button. |

# Segmented button

[Segmented buttons](https://m3.material.io/components/segmented-buttons)
help people select options, switch views, or sort elements.

*   [Design article](https://m3.material.io/components/segmented-buttons) 
*   [API Documentation](#api)
*   [Source code](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/tree/main/segmentedbutton)
    

This follows Jetpack Compose Material 3 (`SegmentedButton`,
`SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow`, `MultiChoiceSegmentedButtonRow`,
`OutlinedSegmentedButtonTokens`).

For a row of separate buttons that change shape when pressed, the Expressive
alternative, use a connected [button group](button-group.md).

## Usage

Put two to five `petal-segmented-button`s in a `petal-segmented-button-set`.
By default one button is selected at a time, and a selected button shows a
checkmark before its label.

```html
<petal-segmented-button-set aria-label="Range">
  <petal-segmented-button label="Day" selected></petal-segmented-button>
  <petal-segmented-button label="Week"></petal-segmented-button>
  <petal-segmented-button label="Month"></petal-segmented-button>
</petal-segmented-button-set>
```

Listen for `segmented-button-set-selection`; its `detail` has the `button`,
whether it is `selected`, and its `index`.

```js
set.addEventListener('segmented-button-set-selection', (event) => {
  console.log(event.detail.index, event.detail.selected);
});
```

### Multiselect

With `multiselect`, each button turns on and off by itself.

```html
<petal-segmented-button-set multiselect aria-label="Price">
  <petal-segmented-button label="$" selected></petal-segmented-button>
  <petal-segmented-button label="$$" selected></petal-segmented-button>
  <petal-segmented-button label="$$$"></petal-segmented-button>
  <petal-segmented-button label="$$$$"></petal-segmented-button>
</petal-segmented-button-set>
```

### Icons

An icon in the `icon` slot shows while the button is not selected; when it is
selected, the checkmark takes its place. Use `no-checkmark` to keep the icon,
for example on icon-only buttons.

```html
<petal-segmented-button-set aria-label="Travel mode">
  <petal-segmented-button label="Walk">
    <petal-icon slot="icon">directions_walk</petal-icon>
  </petal-segmented-button>
  <petal-segmented-button label="Transit" selected>
    <petal-icon slot="icon">train</petal-icon>
  </petal-segmented-button>
</petal-segmented-button-set>

<petal-segmented-button-set aria-label="Theme">
  <petal-segmented-button no-checkmark aria-label="Dark">
    <petal-icon slot="icon">dark_mode</petal-icon>
  </petal-segmented-button>
  <petal-segmented-button no-checkmark aria-label="Light" selected>
    <petal-icon slot="icon">light_mode</petal-icon>
  </petal-segmented-button>
</petal-segmented-button-set>
```

### Width

A set is as wide as its content, with every button as wide as the widest one.
Give the set a width, such as `width: 100%`, to stretch the buttons equally.

## Accessibility

Give the set an `aria-label` that names the choice. A single-select set is a
radio group: only the selected button is in the tab order, and the arrow keys
select the next or previous button. In a multiselect set, every button is a
toggle button in the tab order. Icon-only buttons need an `aria-label`.

## Compose behavior

*   Buttons are at least 58dp wide and 40dp high, with 12dp of padding at the
    sides, the LabelLarge type and an 18dp icon 8dp before the label.
*   The outlines (1dp, outline color) overlap; only the ends of the row are
    rounded, with the full shape. The selected button is drawn over its
    neighbours.
*   Selected: secondary-container with on-secondary-container content.
*   The checkmark grows from its bottom start corner on the fast spatial
    spring and fades in on the default effects spring, and goes at once. The
    space for it is always there; without it, the label moves back to the
    center, sliding on the fast spatial spring. With an icon, the icon and the
    checkmark cross-fade.

## Theming

Segmented buttons support [Material theming](../theming/README.md) and can be
customized in terms of color, typography and shape.

### Tokens

Token                                               | Default value
--------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------
`--md-segmented-button-selected-container-color`    | `--md-sys-color-secondary-container`
`--md-segmented-button-selected-label-text-color`   | `--md-sys-color-on-secondary-container`
`--md-segmented-button-selected-icon-color`         | `--md-sys-color-on-secondary-container`
`--md-segmented-button-unselected-label-text-color` | `--md-sys-color-on-surface`
`--md-segmented-button-unselected-icon-color`       | `--md-sys-color-on-surface`
`--md-segmented-button-outline-color`               | `--md-sys-color-outline`
`--md-segmented-button-outline-width`               | `1px`
`--md-segmented-button-shape`                       | `--md-sys-shape-corner-full`
`--md-segmented-button-container-height`            | `40px`
`--md-segmented-button-icon-size`                   | `18px`
`--md-segmented-button-label-text-font`             | `--md-sys-typescale-label-large-font`

### Moved from labs

The segmented buttons used to be `petal-outlined-segmented-button` and
`petal-outlined-segmented-button-set` in `petal-elements/labs/`. Those modules
still define the old tags, as the new elements, until 1.0.

## API

### PetalSegmentedButtonSet <code>&lt;petal-segmented-button-set&gt;</code>

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `multiselect` | `multiselect` | `boolean` | `false` | Allows several buttons to be selected. |
| `buttons` |  | `SegmentedButton[]` | `undefined` |  |

#### Methods

| Method | Parameters | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `getButtonDisabled` | `index` | `boolean` |  |
| `setButtonDisabled` | `index`, `disabled` | `void` |  |
| `getButtonSelected` | `index` | `boolean` |  |
| `setButtonSelected` | `index`, `selected` | `void` |  |

#### Events

| Event | Type | [Bubbles](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/bubbles) | [Composed](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/composed) | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `segmented-button-set-selection` | `CustomEvent<{button: SegmentedButton, selected: boolean, index: number}>` | Yes | Yes | Dispatched when a button is selected programmatically with the `setButtonSelected` method as well as on user interaction. |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| _default_ | The `petal-segmented-button`s. |

### PetalSegmentedButton <code>&lt;petal-segmented-button&gt;</code>

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the button is disabled. |
| `selected` | `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the button is selected. |
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` | The label text. |
| `noCheckmark` | `no-checkmark` | `boolean` | `false` | Hides the checkmark that a selected button shows in front of its label. |
| `selectionRole` |  | `"radio" \| "toggle"` | `'toggle'` | Set by the segmented button set: `radio` in a single-select set, `toggle` in a multiselect set. |
| `tabbable` |  | `boolean` | `true` | Set by the segmented button set: whether the button is in the tab order. |

#### Events

| Event | Type | [Bubbles](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/bubbles) | [Composed](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/composed) | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `segmented-button-interaction` | `Event` | Yes | Yes | Dispatched when the button is clicked. |
| `segmented-button-selected-change` | `Event` | Yes | Yes | Dispatched when `selected` changes, so the set can update which button is in the tab order. |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `icon` | An icon before the label. |
