File: docs/components/date-picker.md

# Date picker

[Date pickers](https://m3.material.io/components/date-pickers)
let people select a date.

*   [Design article](https://m3.material.io/components/date-pickers) 
*   [API Documentation](#api)
*   [Source code](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/tree/main/datepicker)
    

This follows Jetpack Compose Material 3 (`DatePicker`, `DatePickerDialog`,
`DateInput`, `DatePickerModalTokens`). Picking a range of dates
(`DateRangePicker`) is not available yet.

## Usage

`petal-date-picker` is the calendar with its header. Its `value` is an ISO
date (`2026-10-21`), like `<input type="date">`; it is `''` while nothing is
selected. Selecting a date fires `input` and `change`.

```html
<petal-date-picker value="2026-10-21"></petal-date-picker>
```

Swipe the calendar or use the arrows to change the month, and the month and
year button to pick a year. The picker is 360px wide; set a `width` to change
that. `no-header` leaves out the title and the headline, as passing `null`
for them in Compose.

### Dialog

`petal-date-picker-dialog` shows the picker in a modal dialog with Cancel and
OK. The date picked in the dialog is kept only when OK is pressed: then
`value` changes and `change` fires. Open it with `show()` or `open`.

```html
<petal-filled-tonal-button id="pick-date">Pick a date</petal-filled-tonal-button>
<petal-date-picker-dialog id="date-dialog"></petal-date-picker-dialog>

<script type="module">
  const dialog = document.querySelector('#date-dialog');
  document.querySelector('#pick-date').addEventListener('click', () => dialog.show());
  dialog.addEventListener('change', () => console.log(dialog.value));
</script>
```

To fill a text field, as Compose's samples do, open the dialog from the field
and write the confirmed date into it:

```html
<petal-outlined-text-field label="Date" readonly id="date-field">
  <petal-icon-button slot="trailing-icon" id="date-button" aria-label="Pick a date">
    <petal-icon>calendar_today</petal-icon>
  </petal-icon-button>
</petal-outlined-text-field>
<petal-date-picker-dialog id="date-dialog"></petal-date-picker-dialog>

<script type="module">
  const field = document.querySelector('#date-field');
  const dialog = document.querySelector('#date-dialog');
  document.querySelector('#date-button').addEventListener('click', () => dialog.show());
  dialog.addEventListener('change', () => {
    field.value = dialog.valueAsDate
      ? new Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, {dateStyle: 'medium', timeZone: 'UTC'}).format(
          dialog.valueAsDate,
        )
      : '';
  });
</script>
```

The dialog fires `change` only when OK is pressed, and `open`, `opened`,
`close`, `closed` and `cancel` like [`petal-dialog`](dialog.md); `returnValue`
is `confirm` after OK, `dismiss` after Cancel, and empty after Escape or a
click outside. `quick` opens and closes it without the
animation. Labels of the buttons are `confirm-label` and `dismiss-label`.

### Text input

The pencil button switches to a text field for typing the date, and the
calendar button switches back. Start in it with `display-mode="input"`, or
hide the button with `hide-mode-toggle`. The field takes digits only and adds
the locale's separators; it shows Compose's messages for a date that does not
exist, is outside the years, or cannot be selected.

```html
<petal-date-picker display-mode="input" value="2026-10-21"></petal-date-picker>
```

### Limits

`min` and `max` limit the dates that can be picked, and the months and years
shown; without them the years are 1900 to 2100, as in Compose. For other
rules, set `isDateSelectable` to a function that takes an ISO date, as
Compose's `SelectableDates`.

```html
<petal-date-picker value="2026-10-21" min="2026-10-10" max="2026-10-25"></petal-date-picker>

<script type="module">
  // No weekends.
  document.querySelector('petal-date-picker').isDateSelectable = (date) =>
    ![0, 6].includes(new Date(date).getUTCDay());
</script>
```

### Forms

With a `name`, the picker submits its value with its form, like other form
controls.

```html
<form>
  <petal-date-picker name="date"></petal-date-picker>
</form>
```

### Language

Month and weekday names, the headline and the typed date format come from
`Intl` for the `locale` attribute, or else the closest `lang` attribute, or
else the browser's language. The week starts on the locale's first day; set
`first-day-of-week` (0 for Sunday) to change it.

The fixed texts are English, as Compose's defaults. Replace the visible ones
with attributes (`picker-title`, `picker-headline`, `input-title`,
`input-headline`, `input-label`, and on the dialog `confirm-label` and
`dismiss-label`), and the read-out and error texts with `messages`:

```html
<petal-date-picker-dialog
    lang="zh-CN"
    picker-title="选择日期"
    picker-headline="所选日期"
    input-title="选择日期"
    input-headline="输入的日期"
    input-label="日期"
    confirm-label="确定"
    dismiss-label="取消"></petal-date-picker-dialog>

<script type="module">
  document.querySelector('petal-date-picker-dialog').messages = {
    switchToInputMode: '切换到文字输入',
    switchToCalendarMode: '切换到日历',
    previousMonth: '上个月',
    nextMonth: '下个月',
    today: '今天',
    invalidPattern: '日期格式应为 %1',
    invalidYearRange: '日期应在 %1 年至 %2 年之间',
    invalidNotAllowed: '不能选择 %1',
  };
</script>
```

## Accessibility

The calendar is a grid: one day is in the tab order, the arrow keys move by
day and week, Home and End go to the start and end of the week, Page Up and
Page Down to the previous and next month (with Shift, year), and moving past
the first or last day turns the month. Each day is read with its full date,
and today says so. The headline announces the selected date. In the year
grid, the arrow keys move between years and Escape goes back to the days.

## Compose behavior

*   The picker is 360dp wide on surface-container-high. The header is at least
    120dp: the title in LabelLarge, the headline in HeadlineLarge, and the
    mode button, over a divider.
*   The month row is 56dp high. Weekday letters and days sit in 48dp cells,
    six rows; a day is a 40dp circle in BodyLarge: primary when selected, a
    1dp primary outline and primary text for today, 38% when it cannot be
    picked.
*   The months slide: the arrows on the default spring (no bounce), a swipe on
    the default effects spring, going to the next month on a fling or past
    half the width.
*   The year grid has three 72 by 36dp years per row, 16dp apart, and unfolds
    downwards over the calendar on the default effects spring.
*   Switching to text input slides the field up from below and fades it in
    while the calendar fades out and moves 48dp up, on the default spatial
    and effects springs; the height follows.
*   The dialog is 360dp wide and at most 568dp high, with the extra large
    shape; the buttons are 8dp apart, 6dp from the end and 8dp from the
    bottom.

## Theming

Date pickers support [Material theming](../theming/README.md) and can be
customized in terms of color, typography and shape.

### Tokens

Token                                                  | Default value
------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------
`--md-date-picker-container-color`                     | `--md-sys-color-surface-container-high`
`--md-date-picker-container-shape`                     | `--md-sys-shape-corner-extra-large`
`--md-date-picker-header-headline-color`               | `--md-sys-color-on-surface-variant`
`--md-date-picker-header-supporting-text-color`        | `--md-sys-color-on-surface-variant`
`--md-date-picker-weekdays-label-text-color`           | `--md-sys-color-on-surface`
`--md-date-picker-date-unselected-label-text-color`    | `--md-sys-color-on-surface`
`--md-date-picker-date-selected-container-color`       | `--md-sys-color-primary`
`--md-date-picker-date-selected-label-text-color`      | `--md-sys-color-on-primary`
`--md-date-picker-date-today-label-text-color`         | `--md-sys-color-primary`
`--md-date-picker-date-today-container-outline-color`  | `--md-sys-color-primary`
`--md-date-picker-selection-year-selected-container-color` | `--md-sys-color-primary`
`--md-date-picker-navigation-content-color`            | `--md-sys-color-on-surface-variant`
`--md-date-picker-divider-color`                       | `--md-sys-color-outline-variant`

## API

### PetalDatePicker <code>&lt;petal-date-picker&gt;</code>

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `value` | `string` | `''` | The selected date, as an ISO date (`2026-10-21`), or `''`. |
| `min` | `min` | `string` | `''` | The earliest date that can be selected, as an ISO date. |
| `max` | `max` | `string` | `''` | The latest date that can be selected, as an ISO date. |
| `locale` | `locale` | `string` | `''` | The locale for month and weekday names, the date format and the first day of the week. Defaults to the closest `lang` attribute or the browser's language. |
| `firstDayOfWeek` | `first-day-of-week` | `number` | `undefined` | The first day of the week, 0 for Sunday to 6 for Saturday. Defaults to the locale's. |
| `displayMode` | `display-mode` | `DatePickerDisplayMode` | `'picker'` | `picker` shows the calendar, `input` a text field. |
| `hideModeToggle` | `hide-mode-toggle` | `boolean` | `false` | Hides the button that switches between the calendar and the text field. |
| `pickerTitle` | `picker-title` | `string` | `'Select date'` | The title above the headline in calendar mode. |
| `inputTitle` | `input-title` | `string` | `'Select date'` | The title above the headline in text input mode. |
| `pickerHeadline` | `picker-headline` | `string` | `'Selected date'` | The headline in calendar mode while no date is selected. |
| `inputHeadline` | `input-headline` | `string` | `'Entered date'` | The headline in text input mode while no date is entered. |
| `inputLabel` | `input-label` | `string` | `'Date'` | The text field's label in text input mode. |
| `noHeader` | `no-header` | `boolean` | `false` | Hides the title and the headline, leaving only the calendar. |
| `isDateSelectable` |  | `(date: string) => boolean` | `undefined` | Whether a date can be selected, as Compose's `SelectableDates`. Called with ISO dates between `min` and `max`. |
| `messages` |  | `DatePickerMessages` | `{}` | Replaces some of the read-out and error texts. |
| `name` | `name` | `string` | `undefined` | The HTML name to use in form submission. |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Whether or not the element is disabled. |
| `valueAsDate` |  | `Date` | `undefined` |  |
| `form` |  | `HTMLFormElement` | `undefined` | The associated form element with which this element's value will submit. |
| `labels` |  | `NodeList` | `undefined` | The labels this element is associated with. |

#### Methods

| Method | Parameters | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `showMonthOf` | `date` | `void` | Shows the month that has the given ISO date. |
| `formResetCallback` | _None_ | `void` |  |
| `formStateRestoreCallback` | `state` | `void` |  |

#### Events

| Event | Type | [Bubbles](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/bubbles) | [Composed](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/composed) | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Event` | Yes | Yes | The selection changed. |
| `change` | `Event` | Yes | No | The selection changed. |

### PetalDatePickerDialog <code>&lt;petal-date-picker-dialog&gt;</code>

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `open` | `boolean` | `false` | Opens the dialog when `true`, closes it when `false`. |
| `value` | `value` | `string` | `''` | The confirmed date, as an ISO date (`2026-10-21`), or `''`. |
| `min` | `min` | `string` | `''` | The earliest date that can be selected, as an ISO date. |
| `max` | `max` | `string` | `''` | The latest date that can be selected, as an ISO date. |
| `locale` | `locale` | `string` | `''` | The locale; see `petal-date-picker`. |
| `firstDayOfWeek` | `first-day-of-week` | `number` | `undefined` | The first day of the week, 0 for Sunday to 6 for Saturday. |
| `displayMode` | `display-mode` | `DatePickerDisplayMode` | `'picker'` | `picker` shows the calendar, `input` a text field. |
| `hideModeToggle` | `hide-mode-toggle` | `boolean` | `false` | Hides the button that switches between the calendar and the text field. |
| `pickerTitle` | `picker-title` | `string` | `'Select date'` | The title above the headline in calendar mode. |
| `inputTitle` | `input-title` | `string` | `'Select date'` | The title above the headline in text input mode. |
| `pickerHeadline` | `picker-headline` | `string` | `'Selected date'` | The headline in calendar mode while no date is selected. |
| `inputHeadline` | `input-headline` | `string` | `'Entered date'` | The headline in text input mode while no date is entered. |
| `inputLabel` | `input-label` | `string` | `'Date'` | The text field's label in text input mode. |
| `confirmLabel` | `confirm-label` | `string` | `'OK'` | The confirm button's label. |
| `dismissLabel` | `dismiss-label` | `string` | `'Cancel'` | The dismiss button's label. |
| `quick` | `quick` | `boolean` | `false` | Skips the opening and closing animations. |
| `isDateSelectable` |  | `(date: string) => boolean` | `undefined` | Whether a date can be selected; see `petal-date-picker`. |
| `messages` |  | `DatePickerMessages` | `{}` | Replaces some of the read-out and error texts. |
| `returnValue` |  | `string` | `undefined` |  |

#### Methods

| Method | Parameters | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `show` | _None_ | `Promise<void>` | Opens the dialog. Resolves once it has opened. |
| `close` | `returnValue` | `Promise<void>` | Closes the dialog. Resolves once it has closed. |

#### Events

| Event | Type | [Bubbles](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/bubbles) | [Composed](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/composed) | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `Event` | No | No | The dialog is opening, before any animations. --cancelable |
| `opened` | `Event` | No | No | The dialog has opened, after any animations. |
| `close` | `Event` | No | No | The dialog is closing, before any animations. --cancelable |
| `closed` | `Event` | No | No | The dialog has closed, after any animations. |
| `cancel` | `Event` | No | No | The dialog was canceled with Escape or by clicking outside it. --cancelable |
| `change` | `Event` | Yes | No | A date was confirmed with OK. |

# Time picker

[Time pickers](https://m3.material.io/components/time-pickers)
let people select a time.

*   [Design article](https://m3.material.io/components/time-pickers) 
*   [API Documentation](#api)
*   [Source code](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/tree/main/timepicker)
    

This follows Jetpack Compose Material 3 (`TimePicker`, `TimeInput`,
`TimePickerDialog`, `TimePickerTokens`, `TimeInputTokens`). The Expressive
styles (the vibrant colors and shapes, and the scroll wheel `TimeScroll`) are
not available yet.

## Usage

`petal-time-picker` shows the hour and minute, an AM and PM toggle in 12-hour
time, and a clock dial. Its `value` is a 24-hour time (`14:30`), like
`<input type="time">`; it is `''` until a time is set, while the picker shows
00:00. Changing the time fires `input` and `change`.

```html
<petal-time-picker value="14:30"></petal-time-picker>
```

Tap or drag on the dial to set the hour; the dial then shows the minutes. Tap
the hour or minute above it to choose which the dial sets (`selection`). A
tap sets the closest hour or five minutes; a drag sets any minute.

### 12 and 24 hours

The hour cycle follows the locale (from `locale`, the closest `lang`
attribute, or the browser's language): 12 hours for `en-US`, 24 for `de`,
`zh` or `ja`. Set `hour-cycle="12"` or `"24"` to choose. In 24 hours the
hours from 12 sit on an inner circle of the dial.

```html
<petal-time-picker hour-cycle="24" value="14:30"></petal-time-picker>
```

### Layout

`layout="vertical"` puts the dial below the time, `layout="horizontal"`
beside it. The default, `auto`, is horizontal in a landscape viewport less than
600px high (a phone on its side), as Compose picks by orientation; there the
dial is 256px, or 238px and 200px in viewports less than 384px and 330px high.

### Text input

`display-mode="input"` shows two text fields instead of the dial, as Compose's
`TimeInput`. They take digits only, move from the hour to the minute as soon
as the hour is clear, and show Compose's errors for a number out of range.

```html
<petal-time-picker display-mode="input" value="09:05"></petal-time-picker>
```

In the dialog, a button switches between the dial and the text fields;
`hide-mode-toggle` removes it. `is24Hour` reads whether the picker uses 24
hours (from `hour-cycle` or the locale).

### Dialog

`petal-time-picker-dialog` shows the picker in a modal dialog with a title, a
button that switches between the dial and the text fields, and Cancel and OK.
The time is kept only when OK is pressed: then `value` changes and `change`
fires. Open it with `show()` or `open`.

```html
<petal-filled-tonal-button id="pick-time">Pick a time</petal-filled-tonal-button>
<petal-time-picker-dialog id="time-dialog" value="07:45"></petal-time-picker-dialog>

<script type="module">
  const dialog = document.querySelector('#time-dialog');
  document.querySelector('#pick-time').addEventListener('click', () => dialog.show());
  dialog.addEventListener('change', () => console.log(dialog.value));
</script>
```

The dialog fires `change` only when OK is pressed, and `open`, `opened`,
`close`, `closed` and `cancel` like [`petal-dialog`](dialog.md); `returnValue`
is `confirm` after OK, `dismiss` after Cancel, and empty after Escape or a
click outside. `quick` opens and closes it without the
animation. Labels of the buttons are `confirm-label` and `dismiss-label`.

### Forms

With a `name`, the picker submits its value with its form.

### Language

Numbers and the AM and PM labels come from `Intl` for the locale; set
`am-label` and `pm-label` to change them. The other texts are English, as
Compose's defaults: replace the dialog's with `picker-title`, `input-title`,
`confirm-label`, `dismiss-label`, `input-mode-label` and `picker-mode-label`,
and the picker's read-out, label and error texts with `messages`:

```html
<petal-time-picker-dialog
    lang="zh-CN"
    picker-title="选择时间"
    input-title="输入时间"
    confirm-label="确定"
    dismiss-label="取消"></petal-time-picker-dialog>

<script type="module">
  document.querySelector('petal-time-picker-dialog').messages = {
    hour: '时',
    minute: '分',
    hour24Error: '小时应为 0–23',
    minuteError: '分钟应为 0–59',
    selectHour: '选择小时',
    selectMinute: '选择分钟',
    hour24Suffix: '%1 时',
    minuteSuffix: '%1 分',
  };
</script>
```

## Accessibility

The hour and minute are radio buttons that choose what the dial sets; AM and
PM are a radio group. On the dial, one number is in the tab order: the arrow
keys move around the dial, and Enter or Space picks the focused number. The
text fields are named "Hour" and "Minute" and announce their errors.

## Compose behavior

*   The hour and minute are 96 by 80dp in DisplayLarge, primary-container
    when selected, with a 24dp colon. The AM and PM toggle is 52 by 80dp
    (216 by 38dp below the time when horizontal): two buttons 4dp apart that
    turn from round to 12dp corners when checked, on the fast spatial spring.
*   The dial is 256dp on surface-container-highest, 36dp below the time,
    with numbers on circles 101 and 69/256 across. The 48dp primary handle
    sits on a 2dp track from an 8dp center, and the number under it shows in
    on-primary.
*   A tap moves the handle to the closest hour or five minutes on the default
    spatial spring; a drag follows the pointer and settles on the minute. After
    an hour is tapped, the dial shows minutes 100ms later; the two faces
    cross-fade on the default effects spring.
*   In text input, the fields are 96 by 72dp in DisplayMedium, outlined while
    selected, with BodySmall supporting text 7dp below.
*   The dialog's title is LabelMedium, 24dp from the top and start with 20dp
    below it, and the actions are 8dp apart with 24dp below.

## Theming

Time pickers support [Material theming](../theming/README.md).

### Tokens

Token                                                    | Default value
-------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------
`--md-time-picker-clock-dial-color`                      | `--md-sys-color-surface-container-highest`
`--md-time-picker-clock-dial-selector-handle-container-color` | `--md-sys-color-primary`
`--md-time-picker-clock-dial-selected-label-text-color`  | `--md-sys-color-on-primary`
`--md-time-picker-clock-dial-unselected-label-text-color` | `--md-sys-color-on-surface`
`--md-time-picker-time-selector-selected-container-color` | `--md-sys-color-primary-container`
`--md-time-picker-time-selector-selected-label-text-color` | `--md-sys-color-on-primary-container`
`--md-time-picker-time-selector-unselected-container-color` | `--md-sys-color-surface-container-highest`
`--md-time-picker-period-selector-selected-container-color` | `--md-sys-color-primary-container`
`--md-time-picker-period-selector-unselected-container-color` | `--md-sys-color-surface-container-lowest`
`--md-time-picker-clock-dial-container-size`             | `256px`

## API

### PetalTimePicker <code>&lt;petal-time-picker&gt;</code>

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `value` | `string` | `''` | The time, as `HH:MM` in 24 hours (`14:30`), or `''` for none yet. |
| `displayMode` | `display-mode` | `TimePickerDisplayMode` | `'picker'` | `picker` shows the clock dial, `input` text fields. |
| `hourCycle` | `hour-cycle` | `"" \| "12" \| "24"` | `''` | `12` or `24` hours. Defaults to the locale's: 24 hours for `de` or `zh`, 12 for `en-US`. |
| `locale` | `locale` | `string` | `''` | The locale for numbers, AM and PM and the hour cycle. Defaults to the closest `lang` attribute or the browser's language. |
| `layout` | `layout` | `TimePickerLayout` | `'auto'` | `vertical` (the dial below the time), `horizontal` (beside it), or `auto`: horizontal in a landscape viewport less than 600px high. |
| `amLabel` | `am-label` | `string` | `''` | The AM label. Defaults to the locale's. |
| `pmLabel` | `pm-label` | `string` | `''` | The PM label. Defaults to the locale's. |
| `messages` |  | `TimePickerMessages` | `{}` | Replaces some of the read-out and shown texts. |
| `selection` | `selection` | `TimePickerSelection` | `'hour'` | Which number the dial sets. |
| `name` | `name` | `string` | `undefined` | The HTML name to use in form submission. |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Whether or not the element is disabled. |
| `is24Hour` |  | `boolean` | `undefined` |  |
| `form` |  | `HTMLFormElement` | `undefined` | The associated form element with which this element's value will submit. |
| `labels` |  | `NodeList` | `undefined` | The labels this element is associated with. |

#### Methods

| Method | Parameters | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `formResetCallback` | _None_ | `void` |  |
| `formStateRestoreCallback` | `state` | `void` |  |

| Event | Type | [Bubbles](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/bubbles) | [Composed](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/composed) | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Event` | Yes | Yes | The time changed. |
| `change` | `Event` | Yes | No | The time changed. |

### PetalTimePickerDialog <code>&lt;petal-time-picker-dialog&gt;</code>

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `open` | `boolean` | `false` | Opens the dialog when `true`, closes it when `false`. |
| `value` | `value` | `string` | `''` | The confirmed time, as `HH:MM`, or `''`. |
| `displayMode` | `display-mode` | `TimePickerDisplayMode` | `'picker'` | `picker` shows the clock dial, `input` text fields. |
| `hourCycle` | `hour-cycle` | `"" \| "12" \| "24"` | `''` | `12` or `24` hours; defaults to the locale's. |
| `locale` | `locale` | `string` | `''` | The locale; see `petal-time-picker`. |
| `layout` | `layout` | `TimePickerLayout` | `'auto'` | The picker's layout; see `petal-time-picker`. |

| `inputTitle` | `input-title` | `string` | `'Enter Time'` | The title with the text fields. |

| `pickerModeLabel` | `picker-mode-label` | `string` | `'Switch to clock mode'` | The mode button's name with the text fields. |
| `amLabel` | `am-label` | `string` | `''` | The AM label; see `petal-time-picker`. |
| `pmLabel` | `pm-label` | `string` | `''` | The PM label; see `petal-time-picker`. |
| `quick` | `quick` | `boolean` | `false` | Skips the opening and closing animations. |
| `messages` |  | `TimePickerMessages` | `{}` | Replaces some of the picker's texts. |
| `returnValue` |  | `string` | `undefined` |  |

#### Methods

| Method | Parameters | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `show` | _None_ | `Promise<void>` | Opens the dialog. Resolves once it has opened. |
| `close` | `returnValue` | `Promise<void>` | Closes the dialog. Resolves once it has closed. |

#### Events

| Event | Type | [Bubbles](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/bubbles) | [Composed](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/composed) | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `Event` | No | No | The dialog is opening, before any animations. --cancelable |
| `opened` | `Event` | No | No | The dialog has opened, after any animations. |
| `close` | `Event` | No | No | The dialog is closing, before any animations. --cancelable |
| `closed` | `Event` | No | No | The dialog has closed, after any animations. |
| `cancel` | `Event` | No | No | The dialog was canceled with Escape or by clicking outside it. --cancelable |
| `change` | `Event` | Yes | No | A time was confirmed with OK. |

File: docs/components/progress.md

# Progress indicators

[Progress indicators](https://m3.material.io/components/progress-indicators)
show that something is loading or being processed, and how far it has got when
that is known.

There are two types of progress indicators: linear and circular.

*   [Design article](https://m3.material.io/components/progress-indicators)
    
*   [API Documentation](#api)
*   [Source code](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/tree/main/progress)
    

## Types

1.  [Circular progress](#circular-progress)
1.  [Linear progress](#linear-progress)

## Usage

Progress indicators may be determinate to show progress, or indeterminate for an
unspecified amount of progress.

```html
<petal-circular-progress value="0.75"></petal-circular-progress>
<petal-circular-progress indeterminate></petal-circular-progress>

<petal-linear-progress indeterminate></petal-linear-progress>
<petal-linear-progress value="0.5"></petal-linear-progress>
```

### Four colors

Indeterminate progress indicators may cycle between four colors (primary,
primary container, tertiary, and tertiary container by default).

```html
<petal-circular-progress four-color indeterminate></petal-circular-progress>
<petal-linear-progress four-color indeterminate></petal-linear-progress>
```

## Accessibility

Add an
[`aria-label`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-label)
attribute to progress indicators to give them a descriptive name.

```html
<petal-circular-progress value="0.5" aria-label="Page refresh progress"></petal-circular-progress>

<petal-linear-progress value="0.5" aria-label="Download progress"></petal-linear-progress>
```

## Circular progress

Circular progress indicators display progress by animating along an invisible
circular track in a clockwise direction.

```html
<petal-circular-progress indeterminate></petal-circular-progress>
<petal-circular-progress value="0.6"></petal-circular-progress>
```

Circular indicators follow Jetpack Compose Material 3
(`CircularProgressIndicator`): 40px with a 4px stroke and round caps. A
determinate indicator starts at 12 o'clock with its track
(`--md-sys-color-secondary-container`) after a 4px gap. The indeterminate
indicator has no track; it turns 1080 degrees in 6 seconds plus a quarter turn
every 1.5 seconds while its arc grows from 10% to 87% of the circle and back.

### Wavy circular

`wavy` draws the indicator as a wave around the circle
(`CircularWavyProgressIndicator`): 48px, waves of about 15px (as many as fit
around the circle) that move one wavelength per second, and the track after a
4px gap, also when indeterminate. Determinate waves flatten below 10% and from
95%. With `prefers-reduced-motion`, the wave does not move.

```html
<petal-circular-progress wavy indeterminate></petal-circular-progress>
<petal-circular-progress wavy value="0.6"></petal-circular-progress>
```

## Linear progress

Linear progress indicators display progress by animating along the length of a
fixed, visible track.

```html
<petal-linear-progress indeterminate></petal-linear-progress>
<petal-linear-progress value="0.6"></petal-linear-progress>
```

Linear indicators follow Jetpack Compose Material 3 (`LinearProgressIndicator`):
4px lines with round caps, the track (`--md-sys-color-secondary-container`)
after a 4px gap, and a 4px stop indicator at the end of a determinate
indicator. The indeterminate indicator moves two lines along the track, with
the same gaps. For a thicker indicator (Material 3 Expressive's 8px), set
`--md-linear-progress-track-height`; the gap stays 4px and the stop indicator
4px.

```html
<petal-linear-progress value="0.6" style="--md-linear-progress-track-height: 8px"></petal-linear-progress>
```

### Animating value changes

Like Compose's indicators, an indicator jumps to a new `value`. With
`animate-value`, it moves there on the slow spatial spring of the motion scheme
instead, which overshoots a little (a petal-elements option for linear and
circular, flat and wavy indicators). A value that changes on the way is
followed from where the indicator is; with `prefers-reduced-motion` it jumps.

```html
<petal-linear-progress animate-value max="100" value="71"></petal-linear-progress>
```

### Buffer

Linear progress indicators may show a buffer to communicate both determinate and
indeterminate progress. The progress bar and track represent known progress
while the buffer dots represent unknown progress.

```html
<petal-linear-progress value="0.5" buffer="0.8"></petal-linear-progress>
```

### Wavy

`wavy` draws the indicator as a wave, as in Material 3 Expressive (Jetpack
Compose `LinearWavyProgressIndicator`): 10px high, 4px strokes with round caps,
a 4px gap before the track and a stop dot at its end. Indeterminate waves are
20px long; determinate waves are 40px long and flatten below 10% and from 95%.
The wave moves one wavelength per second. `buffer` and `four-color` do not
apply.

```html
<petal-linear-progress wavy indeterminate></petal-linear-progress>
<petal-linear-progress wavy value="0.6"></petal-linear-progress>
```

Wavy indicators use `--md-linear-progress-wavy-active-indicator-color`
(`--md-sys-color-primary`) and `--md-linear-progress-wavy-track-color`
(`--md-sys-color-secondary-container`), from Compose's
`ProgressIndicatorTokens`. With `prefers-reduced-motion`, the wave does not
move.

## Theming

Progress indicators supports [Material theming](../theming/README.md) and can be
customized in terms of color.

### Circular progress tokens

Token                                           | Default value
----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------
`--md-circular-progress-active-indicator-color` | `--md-sys-color-primary`
`--md-circular-progress-track-color`            | `--md-sys-color-secondary-container`
`--md-circular-progress-size`                   | `40px`
`--md-circular-progress-wavy-size`              | `48px`
`--md-circular-progress-active-indicator-width` | `4px`

> Note: the active indicator width is drawn in a 40px box that scales with
> `--md-circular-progress-size`.

*   [All tokens](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/blob/main/progress/internal/_circular-progress.scss)
    

### Linear progress tokens

Token                                          | Default value
---------------------------------------------- | -------------
`--md-linear-progress-track-color`             | `--md-sys-color-secondary-container`
`--md-linear-progress-track-height`            | `4px`
`--md-linear-progress-track-shape`             | `--md-sys-shape-corner-full`
`--md-linear-progress-active-indicator-color`  | `--md-sys-color-primary`
`--md-linear-progress-active-indicator-height` | `--md-linear-progress-track-height`

*   [All tokens](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/blob/main/tokens/_md-comp-linear-progress.scss)
    

## API

### PetalLinearProgress <code>&lt;petal-linear-progress&gt;</code>

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `buffer` | `buffer` | `number` | `0` | Buffer amount to display, a fraction between 0 and `max`. If the value is 0 or negative, the buffer is not displayed. |
| `wavy` | `wavy` | `boolean` | `false` | Draws the indicator as a wave (Material 3 Expressive, Jetpack Compose `LinearWavyProgressIndicator`). Determinate waves flatten below 10% and from 95%. `buffer` and `four-color` do not apply. |
| `value` | `value` | `number` | `0` | Progress to display, a fraction between 0 and `max`. |
| `max` | `max` | `number` | `1` | Maximum progress to display, defaults to 1. |
| `indeterminate` | `indeterminate` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether or not to display indeterminate progress, which gives no indication to how long an activity will take. |
| `fourColor` | `four-color` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether or not to render indeterminate mode using 4 colors instead of one. |
| `animateValue` | `animate-value` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether a change of `value` (or `max`) moves the indicator on the slow spatial spring of the motion scheme, which overshoots a little, instead of jumping to it. From the shown progress, also when the value changes again on the way; without motion with `prefers-reduced-motion`. Compose's indicators jump (a petal-elements option). |

### PetalCircularProgress <code>&lt;petal-circular-progress&gt;</code>

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wavy` | `wavy` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the indicator is wavy (`CircularWavyProgressIndicator`): 48px, the active indicator a wave that moves around the circle. |
| `value` | `value` | `number` | `0` | Progress to display, a fraction between 0 and `max`. |
| `max` | `max` | `number` | `1` | Maximum progress to display, defaults to 1. |
| `indeterminate` | `indeterminate` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether or not to display indeterminate progress, which gives no indication to how long an activity will take. |
| `fourColor` | `four-color` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether or not to render indeterminate mode using 4 colors instead of one. |
| `animateValue` | `animate-value` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether a change of `value` (or `max`) moves the indicator on the slow spatial spring of the motion scheme, which overshoots a little, instead of jumping to it. From the shown progress, also when the value changes again on the way; without motion with `prefers-reduced-motion`. Compose's indicators jump (a petal-elements option). |

File: docs/components/loading-indicator.md

# Loading indicator

[Loading indicators](https://m3.material.io/components/loading-indicator)
show that content is loading, with a shape that morphs as it turns. A Material
3 Expressive component, for waits shorter than about five seconds.

*   [Design article](https://m3.material.io/components/loading-indicator) 
*   [API Documentation](#api)
*   [Source code](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/tree/main/loadingindicator)
    

This follows Jetpack Compose Material 3 (`LoadingIndicator`,
`ContainedLoadingIndicator`, `LoadingIndicatorTokens`). The shapes and the
morphing are a TypeScript port of Android's graphics-shapes library
(`RoundedPolygon`, `Morph`) and Compose's `MaterialShapes`, so they match
Compose exactly.

## Usage

Without `value`, the indicator is indeterminate: seven Material shapes (soft
burst, 9-sided cookie, pentagon, pill, sunny, 4-sided cookie, oval) morph into
each other every 650ms on a spring, each morph adding a quarter turn, while
the whole indicator turns once every 4.666 seconds.

```html
<petal-loading-indicator aria-label="Loading"></petal-loading-indicator>
```

### Contained

`contained` draws the indicator in a primary container, for use on top of
content (`ContainedLoadingIndicator`).

```html
<petal-loading-indicator contained aria-label="Loading"></petal-loading-indicator>
```

### Determinate

With `value` from 0 to 1, a circle morphs into a soft burst as the value grows,
turning half a turn backward.

```html
<petal-loading-indicator value="0.5" aria-label="Uploading"></petal-loading-indicator>
```

## Accessibility

The indicator is a `progressbar`, with `aria-valuenow` when determinate. Give
it an `aria-label` that says what is loading.

With `prefers-reduced-motion`, the indeterminate indicator keeps one shape and
only turns. Compose does not change the animation; this is a petal-elements
choice.

## Theming

Loading indicators support [Material theming](../theming/README.md). Every
token of Compose's `LoadingIndicatorTokens` is a `--md-loading-indicator-*`
custom property. The container size also scales the shape.

### Tokens

Token                                            | Default value
------------------------------------------------ | -------------
`--md-loading-indicator-active-indicator-color`  | `--md-sys-color-primary`
`--md-loading-indicator-contained-active-color`  | `--md-sys-color-on-primary-container`
`--md-loading-indicator-contained-container-color` | `--md-sys-color-primary-container`
`--md-loading-indicator-container-width`         | `48px`
`--md-loading-indicator-container-height`        | `48px`

*   [All tokens](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/blob/main/tokens/versions/compose/values/_md-comp-loading-indicator.scss)
    

## API

### PetalLoadingIndicator <code>&lt;petal-loading-indicator&gt;</code>

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `value` | `number` | `undefined` | Progress from 0 to 1. When not set, the indicator is indeterminate. |
| `contained` | `contained` | `boolean` | `false` | Draws the indicator in a primary container (ContainedLoadingIndicator). |

File: docs/components/pull-to-refresh.md

# Pull to refresh

Pull to refresh lets people reload content by pulling it down from the top.
The indicator is the petal-elements flower: it blooms as you pull and spins
while refreshing.

*   [API Documentation](#api)
*   [Source code](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/tree/main/pulltorefresh)
    

This component is petal-elements' own and is not part of Material 3.

## Usage

`<petal-pull-to-refresh>` is the scroll container for its content, so give it a
height. Pulling down at the top shows the indicator:

1.  While pulling, the four petals grow out of the center one after another,
    then the center appears and the flower turns. It blooms once the pull is
    far enough.
2.  Releasing past that point sets `refreshing` and fires `refresh`. The flower
    spins and its petals breathe.
3.  Set `refreshing` back to `false` when the content is loaded. The petals fold
    into the center and the indicator slides away.

```html
<petal-pull-to-refresh id="feed" style="height: 400px">
  <petal-list>
    <petal-list-item>Inbox</petal-list-item>
    <petal-list-item>Starred</petal-list-item>
  </petal-list>
</petal-pull-to-refresh>

<script type="module">
  const feed = document.querySelector('#feed');
  feed.addEventListener('refresh', async () => {
    await loadNewItems();
    feed.refreshing = false;
  });
</script>
```

Setting `refreshing` yourself shows the spinning flower without a pull, for
example while the first page loads.

### Page scroll

By default the element is its own scroll container. To keep the page
scrolling as usual (so mobile browsers still hide their address bar, and
`window.scrollY` keeps working), set `scroll-target="page"` and wrap the page
content without giving it a height. Under a sticky top app bar, set
`--md-pull-to-refresh-top-offset` to the bar's height, so the indicator comes
out below it.

```html
<petal-pull-to-refresh scroll-target="page"
    style="--md-pull-to-refresh-top-offset: 64px">
  <petal-top-app-bar headline="Rates"></petal-top-app-bar>
  <main>...</main>
</petal-pull-to-refresh>
```

## Accessibility

Pulling needs touch, so mouse and keyboard users cannot refresh this way. Also
offer another way to refresh, such as a button.

While refreshing, the indicator is a `progressbar` named by `label`
(`"Refreshing"` by default). Otherwise it is hidden from assistive technology.

With `prefers-reduced-motion`, the flower does not turn, spin or breathe; it
fades gently while refreshing.

## Theming

Token                                   | Default value
--------------------------------------- | -------------
`--md-pull-to-refresh-container-color`  | `--md-sys-color-surface-container-high`
`--md-pull-to-refresh-petal-1-color`    | `#f48fb1`
`--md-pull-to-refresh-petal-2-color`    | `#ec407a`
`--md-pull-to-refresh-petal-3-color`    | `#f06292`
`--md-pull-to-refresh-petal-4-color`    | `#f8bbd0`
`--md-pull-to-refresh-center-color`     | `#ffd54f`
`--md-pull-to-refresh-top-offset`       | `0px`

## API

### PetalPullToRefresh <code>&lt;petal-pull-to-refresh&gt;</code>

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `refreshing` | `refreshing` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether a refresh is in progress. Set it to false when it is done. |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Ignores pulls. |
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `'Refreshing'` | Accessible name of the indicator while refreshing. |
| `scrollTarget` | `scroll-target` | `"" \| "page"` | `''` | What scrolls: empty (the default) for the element itself, which then needs a height, or `page` to follow the page scroll, so the whole page does not need to be wrapped in a scroll container. |

#### Events

| Event | Type | [Bubbles](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/bubbles) | [Composed](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/composed) | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `refresh` | `Event` | Yes | Yes | The user pulled past the threshold and released. `refreshing` is already true. |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| _default_ | The content that scrolls and is pulled down. |

File: docs/components/icon.md

# Icon

[Icons](https://m3.material.io/styles/icons/overview)
show common actions and objects as symbols. Material Symbols is a variable icon
font in three styles with adjustable weight, fill, grade and optical size.

*   [Design article](https://m3.material.io/styles/icons) 
*   [API Documentation](#api)
*   [Source code](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/tree/main/icon)
    

## Usage

Icons can be specified by name, unicode code point, or have an `<svg>` child
element.

```html
<petal-icon>settings</petal-icon>
<petal-icon>&#xe834</petal-icon>
<petal-icon><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 48 48"><path d="M10 40V24H4L24 6l10 8.85V9h4v9.55L44 24h-6v16H26.5V28h-5v12Zm3-3h5.5V25h11v12H35V19.95l-11-10-11 10Zm5.5-12h11-11Zm1.25-5.5h8.5q0-1.65-1.275-2.725Q25.7 15.7 24 15.7q-1.7 0-2.975 1.075Q19.75 17.85 19.75 19.5Z"/></svg></petal-icon>
```

The full range of icons can be found on the
[Material Symbols](https://fonts.google.com/icons) font page.

An icon name is text in the page: it can show in search results, text
selection, reader modes, or before the font loads (as `sync_alt`). A code
point is a single private-use character, so it does none of that, and it also
works with a subset font that has no ligatures. Each icon's code point is on
the font page.

Material Symbols icons are available in three styles: **outlined**, **rounded**,
and **sharp**.

In addition, Material Symbols have four adjustable stylistic variable font
attributes called axes. An axis is a typographic term referring to the attribute
of a symbol that can be altered to create visual variations.

Each style symbol contains four axes: **weight**, **fill**, **grade**, and
**optical size**.

The `weight` and `optical size` attributes are handled automatically, but the
`fill` and `grade` attributes are custom to the Material Symbols font, and must
be set with the
[`font-variation-settings`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/font-variation-settings)
property.

### Outlined

Outlined symbols use stroke and fill attributes for a light, clean style that
works well in dense UIs. The stroke weight of outlined icons can be adjusted to
complement or contrast the weight of your typography.

Load the font with

```html
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/icon?family=Material+Symbols+Outlined" rel="stylesheet">
```

### Rounded

Rounded symbols use a corner radius that pairs well with brands that use heavier
typography, curved logos, or circular elements to express their style.

Load the font with

```html
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/icon?family=Material+Symbols+Rounded" rel="stylesheet">
```

To use Rounded icons, set `--md-icon-font` to `'Material Symbols Rounded'`.

### Sharp

Sharp symbols display corners with straight edges, for a crisp style that
remains legible even at smaller scales. These rectangular shapes can support
brand styles that aren’t well-reflected by rounded shapes.

Load the font with

```html
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/icon?family=Material+Symbols+Sharp" rel="stylesheet">
```

To use Sharp icons, set `font-family` to `'Material Symbols Sharp'`.

### Fill

Filled Icons gives you the ability to transition from a more outlined style to a
reversed or more filled style.

A fill attribute can be used to convey a state of transition, such as unfilled
and filled states. Values range from `0` to `1`, with `1` being completely
filled. Along with weight, fill is a primary attribute that impacts the overall
look of a symbol.

Set `filled` to fill an icon. The fill comes from the `--md-icon-fill`
custom property (`0` to `1`), which animates on the default effects spring and
inherits, so a parent can fill its icons, for example when it is selected:

```html
<petal-icon filled>settings</petal-icon>

<style>
  petal-icon-button[aria-expanded='true'] {
    --md-icon-fill: 1;
  }
</style>
```

Icons set the Material Symbols axes with `font-variation-settings: 'FILL'
var(--md-icon-fill)`. To set other axes, such as `GRAD`, set
`font-variation-settings` on the icon itself and include `'FILL'
var(--md-icon-fill)`.

## Accessibility

Icons are mostly intended to be used inside of other components that have
accessibility settings.

If used on their own, Icons should be given an accessible name if they are
focusable. If you use icons by name, they will be announced by screen readers
without any extra steps.

If using codepoints, wrap the codepoint in a `<span>` with an
[`aria-label`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-label)
attribute.

```html
<petal-icon tabindex="-1"><span aria-label="home">&#xe88a</span></petal-icon>
```

If using SVG icons, add an `aria-label` attribute to the SVG element.

```html
<petal-icon tabindex="-1"><svg aria-label="paper airplane" viewBox="0 0 48 48"><path d="M6 40V8l38 16Zm3-4.65L36.2 24 9 12.5v8.4L21.1 24 9 27Zm0 0V12.5 27Z"/></svg></petal-icon>
```

## Theming

### Tokens

Token            | Default value
---------------- | -----------------------------
`--md-icon-font` | `'Material Symbols Outlined'`
`--md-icon-size` | `24px`

*   [All tokens](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/blob/main/tokens/_md-comp-icon.scss)
    

## API

### PetalIcon <code>&lt;petal-icon&gt;</code>

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filled` | `filled` | `boolean` | `false` | Fills the icon (the Material Symbols FILL axis). Changes animate. |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| _default_ | The icon: a Material Symbols ligature name (`search`) or an `<svg>`. |

File: docs/components/elevation.md

# Elevation

[Elevation](https://m3.material.io/styles/elevation)
shows how far a surface sits above another, as a shadow.

Material's elevation system is deliberately limited to just a handful of levels.
This creative constraint means you need to make thoughtful decisions about your
UI’s elevation story.

*   [Design article](https://m3.material.io/styles/elevation) 
*   [API Documentation](#api)
*   [Source code](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/tree/main/elevation)
    

## Usage

Elevation can be set from 0 to 5 using the `--md-elevation-level` CSS custom
property. The elevation will automatically fill the nearest `position: relative`
element's size and shape.

```html
<style>
  .surface {
    position: relative;
    border-radius: 16px;
    height: 64px;
    width: 64px;

    --md-elevation-level: 3;
  }
</style>
<div class="surface">
  <petal-elevation></petal-elevation>
  
</div>
```

### Animation

Shadows may be animated between levels by adding `transition-duration` and
`transition-easing-function` CSS properties.

```html
<style>
  .surface {
    /* ... */
    transition-duration: 250ms;
    transition-timing-function: ease-in-out;

    --md-elevation-level: 3;
  }

  .surface:active {
    --md-elevation-level: 0;
  }
</style>
<div class="surface">
  <petal-elevation></petal-elevation>
  
</div>
```

## Accessibility

Elevation is a visual component and does not have accessibility concerns.

## Theming

Elevation supports [Material theming](../theming/README.md) and can be
customized in terms of color.

### Tokens

Token                         | Default value
----------------------------- | -----------------------
`--md-elevation-level`        | `0`
`--md-elevation-shadow-color` | `--md-sys-color-shadow`

*   [All tokens](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/blob/main/tokens/_md-comp-elevation.scss)
    

### Example

```html
<style>
  .surface {
    position: relative;
    border-radius: 16px;
    height: 64px;
    width: 64px;
  }

  :root {
    --md-elevation-level: 5;
    --md-sys-color-shadow: #006A6A;
  }
</style>
<div class="surface">
  <petal-elevation></petal-elevation>
  
</div>
```

File: docs/components/focus-ring.md

# Focus ring

Focus rings are accessible outlines for components to show keyboard focus.

Focus rings follow the same heuristics as
[`:focus-visible`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:focus-visible)
to determine when they are visible.

*   [API Documentation](#api)
*   [Source code](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/tree/main/focus)
    

## Usage

Focus rings display on keyboard navigation. They may be attached to a control in
one of three ways.

1.  Attached to the parent element

    ```html
    <button style="position: relative">
      <petal-focus-ring style="--md-focus-ring-shape: 8px"></petal-focus-ring>
    </button>
    ```

1.  Attached to a referenced element

    ```html
    <div style="position: relative">
      <petal-focus-ring for="control" style="--md-focus-ring-shape: 8px"></petal-focus-ring>
      <input id="control">
    </div>
    ```

1.  Attached imperatively

    ```html
    <div style="position: relative">
      <petal-focus-ring id="ring" style="--md-focus-ring-shape: 8px"></petal-focus-ring>
      <button id="ring-control"></button>
    </div>
    <script>
      const focusRing = document.querySelector('#ring');
      const control = document.querySelector('#ring-control');
      focusRing.attach(control);
    </script>
    ```

> Note: focus rings must be placed within a `position: relative` container.

### Inward

Focus rings can be changed to animate inwards by adding an `inward` attribute.
This is useful for components like list items.

```html
<button style="position: relative">
  <petal-focus-ring inward style="--md-focus-ring-shape: 8px"></petal-focus-ring>
</button>
```

### Animation

The focus ring animation may be customized or disabled using CSS custom
properties.

```html
<style>
  petal-focus-ring {
    --md-focus-ring-duration: 0s; /* disabled animation */
  }
</style>
```

## Accessibility

Focus rings are visual components and do not have assistive technology
requirements.

## Theming

Focus rings supports [Material theming](../theming/README.md) and can be
customized in terms of color and shape.

### Tokens

Token                   | Default value
----------------------- | --------------------------
`--md-focus-ring-color` | `--md-sys-color-secondary`
`--md-focus-ring-shape` | `--md-sys-shape-corner-full`
`--md-focus-ring-width` | `3px`

*   [All tokens](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/blob/main/tokens/_md-comp-focus-ring.scss)
    

## API

### PetalFocusRing <code>&lt;petal-focus-ring&gt;</code>

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `visible` | `visible` | `boolean` | `false` | Makes the focus ring visible. |
| `inward` | `inward` | `boolean` | `false` | Makes the focus ring animate inwards instead of outwards. |
| `htmlFor` |  | `string` | `undefined` |  |
| `control` |  | `HTMLElement` | `undefined` |  |

#### Methods

| Method | Parameters | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `attach` | `control` | `void` |  |
| `detach` | _None_ | `void` |  |

#### Events

| Event | Type | [Bubbles](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/bubbles) | [Composed](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event/composed) | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `visibility-changed` | `Event` | No | No | Fired whenever `visible` changes. |

File: docs/components/ripple.md

# Ripple

Ripples are
[state layers](https://m3.material.io/foundations/interaction/states/state-layers)
used to communicate the status of a component or interactive element.

A state layer is a semi-transparent covering on an element that indicates its
state. A layer can be applied to an entire element or in a circular shape.

*   [Design article](https://m3.material.io/foundations/interaction/states/state-layers)
    
*   [API Documentation](#api)
*   [Source code](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/tree/main/ripple)
    

## Usage

Ripples display on hover and press pointer interactions. They may be attached to
a control in one of three ways.

1.  Attached to the parent element

    ```html
    <style>
      .container {
        position: relative;
      }
    </style>
    <button class="container">
      <petal-ripple></petal-ripple>
    </button>
    ```

1.  Attached to a referenced element

    ```html
    <style>
      .container {
        position: relative;
      }
    </style>
    <div class="container">
      <petal-ripple for="control"></petal-ripple>
      <input id="control">
    </div>
    ```

1.  Attached imperatively

    ```html
    <style>
      .container {
        position: relative;
      }
    </style>
    <div class="container">
      <petal-ripple id="ripple"></petal-ripple>
      <button id="ripple-control"></button>
    </div>
    <script>
      const ripple = document.querySelector('#ripple');
      const control = document.querySelector('#ripple-control');
      ripple.attach(control);
    </script>
    ```

> Note: ripples must be placed within a `position: relative` container.

### Unbounded

To create an unbounded circular ripple centered on an element, use the following styles.

```css
.container {
  display: flex;
  place-content: center;
  place-items: center;
  position: relative;
}

petal-ripple.unbounded {
  border-radius: 50%;
  inset: unset;
  height: var(--state-layer-size);
  width: var(--state-layer-size);
}
```

```html
<style>
  .container {
    border-radius: 50%;
    height: 32px;
    width: 32px;

    /* Needed for unbounded ripple */
    display: flex;
    place-content: center;
    place-items: center;
    position: relative;
  }

  petal-ripple.unbounded {
    /* Needed for unbounded ripple */
    border-radius: 50%;
    inset: unset;
    height: 64px;
    width: 64px;
  }
</style>
<button class="container">
  <petal-ripple class="unbounded"></petal-ripple>
</button>
```

## Accessibility

Ripples are visual components and do not have assistive technology requirements.

## Theming

Ripples support [Material theming](../theming/README.md) and can be customized
in terms of color.

### Tokens

Token                    | Default value
------------------------ | ------------------------
`--md-ripple-hover-color` | `--md-sys-color-on-surface`
`--md-ripple-pressed-color` | `--md-sys-color-on-surface`

*   [All tokens](https://github.com/Saki340/petal-elements/blob/main/tokens/_md-comp-ripple.scss)
    

## API

### PetalRipple <code>&lt;petal-ripple&gt;</code>

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the ripple. |
| `htmlFor` |  | `string` | `undefined` |  |
| `control` |  | `HTMLElement` | `undefined` |  |

#### Methods

| Method | Parameters | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `attach` | `control` | `void` |  |
| `detach` | _None_ | `void` |  |
